nifty-faces--locked-geometry.title: Faces Built from Boxes
nifty-faces--locked-geometry.question: What can a face built entirely from rectangles show that a drawn face cannot?
nifty-faces--locked-geometry.introduction: Every face here is constructed from stacked and nested rectangles — eye boxes, tooth bars, brow bands — rather than drawn as a continuous form. Moving through seventeen works, the exhibition traces how that rigid geometry is established, loaded with competing marks, and finally pushed to the point where its compartments can no longer hold their contents.
nifty-faces--locked-geometry.closing: Rectangles divide a face into zones. By the final works, those zones are labeled, leaking, and visibly strained — which raises the question of what the geometry was doing in the first place.

chapters.title: The Basic Grammar
chapters.introduction: Three works establish the core structure: a face divided into hard-edged zones, each feature assigned its own rectangular compartment with a distinct interior.

stops.whyHere: The exhibition's threshold: a face framed by a rust-orange inner line and a blue outer line, eyes spiked and glowing amber inside rigid frames, mouth a row of white vertical bars — the locked structure stated plainly.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #63

stops.whyHere: X-marked eye rectangles and stacked horizontal bars echo W001's locked zones, but a flat blue ground and zigzag edges hold the whole structure at a cooler, more diagrammatic remove.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W001 glows warm amber inside a dark teal field, here a flat blue ground and crossed-out eyes push the constructed face toward something colder and more schematic.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #46

stops.whyHere: Stacked eye blocks and a wide tooth bar repeat the compartment logic, but a jagged sawtooth crown and loose white lines crossing every boundary introduce the first visible signs of instability.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The X-eyes of W109 are replaced by banded rectangles, and the purple field gives the structure a heavier ceremonial weight, while the sawtooth crown breaks the strict containment W109 maintained.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #97

chapters.title: Flat Grounds, Direct Address
chapters.introduction: Four works place the rectangular face against a single saturated color, removing spatial depth and pushing the assembled features into unmediated contact with the viewer.

stops.whyHere: Red X eyes in white squares on a burnt-orange field: the flattest, most emblem-like face so far, every mark locked inside its block with almost no marks escaping the boundary.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W116's loose white lines crossing its boundaries are absent here; W042 returns to strict containment, the orange ground pressing everything flush against the picture plane.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #96

stops.whyHere: The same orange field as W042, but crosshatched rectangles replace the bold X eyes, and white scribble lines begin to radiate beyond the face outline, introducing surface restlessness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both share a flat orange ground and sealed eye rectangles, but W051's crosshatching and radiating scribbles introduce a restlessness that W042's clean X marks suppress.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #70

stops.whyHere: Acid yellow-green replaces orange; the left eye box holds a red X while the right holds a horizontal bar, giving the face a slightly asymmetric locked quality, and loose jagged lines now scatter across the entire field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W051's scribbles stayed near the head; here the loose lines cover the whole yellow-green field, making the rigid face structure feel surrounded rather than simply decorated.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #106

stops.whyHere: Yellow presses in from every edge as in W083, but steep diagonal black lines over the eyes and a sealed white horizontal mouth bar pull the geometry inward rather than outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W083's lines scatter across the field; W123 draws them back inward as steep diagonal hatching, tightening the geometry around a face that offers no opening.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #14

chapters.title: Compartments at Capacity
chapters.introduction: Five works fill each rectangular zone with competing marks — crossed lines, spirals, packed strokes — until the interior of every compartment is working against its own boundary.

stops.whyHere: White ovals crossed by red horizontal bars in each eye box, triangular teeth in the mouth zone: compartments packed with competing strokes, each mark holding its brightness against the surrounding noise.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W123's diagonal lines compressed the surface inward; W028 opens the color back up, filling each rectangular zone with layered strokes rather than a single dominant mark.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #39

stops.whyHere: Spiral eye zones pull attention inward while the mouth's packed crosshatch reads as noise against the open teal ground, which gives the density room the darker fields denied.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W028's eye marks were flat ovals with horizontal bars; W060 replaces them with tight concentric spirals, adding a centripetal pull the earlier work's horizontal marks refused.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #54

stops.whyHere: Dense crossing lines fill the eye areas until they read as texture rather than gaze; the compressed mid-face leaves almost no gap between the stacked zones.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W060's spirals still read as eyes; W066 fills its eye boxes so densely with crossing lines that any sense of a directed gaze dissolves into pattern.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #101

stops.whyHere: Cross marks inside rounded-square eye sockets, a dense interior of short color strokes cut by white zigzags: the most modular face yet, each zone a self-contained emblem on a white ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W066's density was built from line alone; W010 introduces short color strokes packed between black scaffolding, giving the interior a chromatic pressure rather than a purely linear one.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #40

stops.whyHere: Zigzag brow bands, stacked rectangles crowding the eye zone, a row of white rounded blocks as a lower jaw: the face reads as a stage set, each zone a separate scene framed top and bottom.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W010's compartments were tightly sealed on a white ground; W020 opens the composition vertically, the striped top and tooth-row bottom framing the dense center like a proscenium arch.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #53

chapters.title: Scaffolding Made Visible
chapters.introduction: Four works pull back from maximum density toward a structural, diagrammatic quality: the face reads as a plan or diagram rather than a presence, and the scaffolding itself becomes the subject.

stops.whyHere: Spring coils bracket the sides, cross-marked ovals sit inside nested rectangles, and the white ground makes the structural logic fully legible — the face as mechanical diagram.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W020's stage-set density gives way to W098's white ground, where the stacked rectangular logic is most exposed and the coil lines at each side make the compression literal.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #51

stops.whyHere: Yellow scaffolding frames a grid of smaller rectangles; three spirals pull inward at different depths while a zigzag mouth band sits flat and wide — diagram and vortex held in the same image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W098's spring coils suggested compression from outside the face; W099 internalises that energy as spirals nested within the yellow frame, pulling inward rather than pressing in from the sides.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #35

stops.whyHere: Three stacked rectangles build a face as compartments: spiral eyes above, a pale loosely scratched mouth below, hot pink and dark maroon pulling the mood in opposite directions across the surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W099's spirals were symmetrically placed within a centred yellow frame; W119 shifts the weight to one side with heavy magenta hatching on the right edge, breaking the bilateral calm.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #31

stops.whyHere: A round face outline breaks the rectangular rule, but the interior is still divided into eye boxes with crossed-circle marks and a scalloped tooth border — the compartment logic persisting inside a curved boundary.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W119's tall rectangular form gives way to a round outline, a visible contrast in silhouette, yet the same bilateral eye-box symmetry and tooth border hold the face to the same constructed logic.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #80

chapters.title: The Frame Under Strain
chapters.introduction: The final two works push the rectangular structure to its limit: marks escape their zones, labels appear on the grid, and the geometry reads as something it can no longer fully organize.

stops.whyHere: Three labeled eye-boxes spelling X, Y, Z make the grid literal; double stacked mouth rectangles and loose lines leaking past the lavender field push the schematic face to its most explicit and unstable form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W131's crossed-circle eye marks were ambiguous; W134 replaces ambiguity with legible letters, turning each eye zone into a labeled grid cell and making the face's constructed logic impossible to overlook.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #76

nifty-faces--radiating-pressure.title: Lines That Cannot Stay Inside
nifty-faces--radiating-pressure.question: When marks escape the face's boundary, what remains to hold the face together?
nifty-faces--radiating-pressure.introduction: Fifteen works share a single observable condition: lines that extend past the face they describe. Some push outward in hard diagonals; others dissolve the boundary until figure and field occupy the same visual register. The exhibition moves from faces where the boundary still holds, through works where the overflow competes equally with the features, to images where the face is readable only through density.
nifty-faces--radiating-pressure.closing: Where the boundary holds, the face is legible. Where it gives way, the marks continue into the field — and what remains is still, just barely, a face. The question is what is doing the holding.

chapters.title: The Boundary Holds
chapters.introduction: Four works where a recognizable face dominates the composition, even as lines press against its edges and begin to extend past them into the surrounding field.

stops.whyHere: Pointed animal ears, scribbled oval eye zones, and bared teeth lock the face in place; loose colored loops spilling into the open teal ground are the first visible sign of outward pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #117

stops.whyHere: A thick black scaffold holds the rectangular head firm against saturated red; the wavy white line above and triangular teeth read as almost orderly, yet crossing lines in magenta, green, and blue flood every interior surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the first work leaks loosely into open teal, this one is hemmed by a hard yellow border — the pressure is comparable but the container is visibly tighter.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #13

stops.whyHere: Squared eye-frames and a wide tooth-filled mouth give the face a mask-like flatness; teal outline loops extending into the red field signal that the boundary is already giving way.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work holds its shape through thick black scaffolding; here flat framing squares replace that scaffold, and the saturated red field pressing in from outside feels more aggressive.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #7

stops.whyHere: A rigid cyan-and-white outline holds a near-square head against dark navy; magenta concentric-ring eyes pull attention inward while ribbon lines of cyan, red, and yellow spill into all four corners.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's red field pushes inward from outside; here the dark navy recedes and the face's own lines are what escape outward into the corners — pressure direction reverses.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #24

chapters.title: Overflow as the Main Event
chapters.introduction: Five works where the lines escaping the face are as visually prominent as the face itself — the boundary and the field competing on equal terms for attention.

stops.whyHere: Mismatched eye heights and a striped mouth anchor the face, but the spiky scribble field pressing inward from every edge competes with the features for attention.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's overflow stays ribbon-like and peripheral; here the scribble mass is dense enough to crowd the face from all sides simultaneously.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #127

stops.whyHere: Red X marks inside heavily cross-hatched oval eyes and a grimace-wide tooth band hold the center, while colored lines spill past the face edge into a jagged, unclosed border.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's scribble field presses inward toward the face; here the lines press outward — direction reverses, but the face is equally contested in both.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #107

stops.whyHere: Hard diagonal wedges shoot to every image edge, breaking the face into shards; two small rectangular eye zones are the only still point in a composition that pulls entirely outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work retains a closed face shape with leaking edges; here closure is abandoned — the diagonals dominate and the face is reconstructed from what remains at center.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #16

stops.whyHere: Looping yellow lines spread like unraveling wire across the upper half while the stacked-block face below holds firm; the hot-pink field and cool layered shapes at right pull in opposite directions.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's overflow is sharp and angular; here hard wedges give way to looping wire — the energy is comparable but the texture shifts from shards to coils.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #30

stops.whyHere: Magenta loops and black scribbles refuse every boundary, spilling into all four corners; a single nested-square eye and a red-arced mouth are the only features holding their position inside the density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work keeps a firm block-face anchoring the lower half; here only one squared eye and a mouth arc remain — the face is already thinning toward its minimum.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #3

chapters.title: Density Without Outline
chapters.introduction: Three works where the face emerges from accumulated marks rather than drawn edges — features readable only because lines pile up more thickly in some areas than others.

stops.whyHere: Layer after layer of short scribble lines accumulate until the face is a site of density; two small dark-outlined eye forms are the only fixed points inside the surrounding noise.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work still has a legible arc-mouth and squared eye; here those anchors reduce to two small dark forms nearly swallowed by the scribble mass.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #9

stops.whyHere: The face is built entirely from looping lines with no solid fills; features emerge only where loops compress most tightly, and the background's own dense magenta scrawl pushes the face forward without a hard edge doing that work.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's scribble lines are short and directional; here long looping coils replace them — the face becomes even less outlined and more accumulated.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #5

stops.whyHere: Pale radiating spikes dissolve the head's boundary into the warm looping background; the tooth-filled mouth with its hard black outlines is the one remaining anchor where figure and field share the same line weight everywhere else.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work holds the face forward through contrast with a busy background; here face and ground use identical line weight, and the boundary nearly disappears.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #25

chapters.title: The Grid Imposed on the Dissolving Face
chapters.introduction: Three works that place rectangular framing or a structural grid over a face already losing its boundary — testing whether geometry can recover what the overflow has dispersed.

stops.whyHere: Four quadrants divide the composition like a grid, but the dividing lines bulge and overlap; two mismatched spiked circles and barred rectangles suggest face-parts arranged rather than drawn as a unified form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work dissolves the face through shared line weight; here a grid attempts to reassemble it — but the grid itself refuses to stay tidy.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #57

stops.whyHere: A tilted rectangular form locks a face-like structure inside a crossing-line grid; spiral eye forms anchor the composition while bars, loose white loops, and dense color hatching press inward around them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work divides into four roughly equal zones; here the whole structure tilts, making the grid feel less like a container and more like another layer of pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #10

stops.whyHere: Strict rectangular framing — two large boxed spiral eyes, one long zigzag-mouth rectangle — holds the composition together even as cyan, yellow, red, and black lines fill every zone including the background with no empty space.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's grid competes with the marks it contains; here the rectangles are the dominant visual fact, the last structural claim the face can make on a fully saturated field.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #12

nifty-faces--mismatched-eyes.title: Two Eyes, Two Systems
nifty-faces--mismatched-eyes.question: When a face's two eyes are built from different shapes or visual logics, what does the rest of the face do?
nifty-faces--mismatched-eyes.introduction: Every face here carries a visible split: two eye zones built from different shapes, different mark systems, or different visual weights. Some differences are subtle — a slight shift in height or framing. Others are total opposites. Moving through this gallery, notice how that single asymmetry changes what the whole face appears to be doing, and whether a mouth full of teeth settles the question or opens another.
nifty-faces--mismatched-eyes.closing: Fifteen faces, none of them symmetrical. Whether the asymmetry reads as alertness, imbalance, or something else may depend entirely on which eye you look at first.

chapters.title: Unequal but Contained
chapters.introduction: These faces hold their asymmetry inside a stable overall structure. The two eye zones differ in mark or color, but the form stays composed — the split is present without tipping into disorder.

stops.whyHere: Two eye zones with different internal rhythms — one coiled, one cross-hatched — sit within a tightly stacked, slab-like form that keeps the tension compressed.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #43

stops.whyHere: A red grid appears over both eye zones, yet warm gold and cool teal beneath them give each side a different temperature, splitting the face through color rather than shape.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W034 uses line density to separate its eyes, here the same grid structure lands on opposite color fields, making the split quieter but just as persistent.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #89

stops.whyHere: Both eyes are small yellow-green discs, but one is surrounded by a wide looping oval frame while the other sits inside a dense rectangular scribble block — the asymmetry is in the framing, not the eyes themselves.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W074 splits its face through color zones beneath a shared structure; W037 keeps both eyes similar in form but wraps each in a different kind of enclosure, a subtler division held inside a face split between pale and dense grounds.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #49

chapters.title: Radiating Against Winding
chapters.introduction: Here the asymmetry becomes structural: one eye expands outward through rings or petals while the other contracts inward through spirals, placing opposite visual logics side by side.

stops.whyHere: A sunflower-like eye radiates orange petals outward on the right; a tight black-and-brown spiral winds inward on the left. The head feels pulled in two directions at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W037's asymmetry lies in framing; here the opposition is more dynamic — one eye that opens outward and one that closes inward, set against a dense, layered head mass.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #98

stops.whyHere: Concentric spoked rings expand from the left eye while dense parallel bars compress the right into a tight column — the most explicit outward-versus-inward opposition in the gallery.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W018 pairs a petal-burst with a spiral; W106 sharpens the contrast to spokes against bars, making the two visual systems feel almost mechanical in their opposition.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #44

stops.whyHere: A single large spiral eye dominates the upper center while the left side holds a rectangular zone of yellow outline and magenta stroke — one eye pulls inward, the other zone pushes outward in flat color.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W106 balances its two opposing eyes symmetrically in the frame; W079 lets the spiral eye overwhelm the composition, making the asymmetry a matter of scale as much as form.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #37

stops.whyHere: The left eye is a wide white circle on black — open and staring — while the right coils into a white spiral. Pink loops stitch the mismatched pair into a single restless surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W079's spiral dominates a flat sky-blue field; W081 places its spiral beside a wide staring circle, and pink line-work connects the two rather than letting them sit apart.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #118

chapters.title: Three Eyes and Other Departures
chapters.introduction: Two faces complicate the count itself — one presents three eye-like forms, another reduces one eye to near-absence. The asymmetry is no longer just left versus right.

stops.whyHere: Three eye-like forms appear: two looping ovals on the left and one larger tilted almond on the right, cooler and more open — the face exceeds the expected pair entirely.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W081's two mismatched eyes are still recognizably a pair; W044 adds a third form, making the count itself part of the asymmetry.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #112

stops.whyHere: One eye swells to fill nearly a quarter of the image; the other shrinks to a small dark circle. The size gap is so extreme the face reads as off-balance before any other feature registers.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W044 multiplies eye forms; W022 reduces one to near-absence while inflating the other, achieving a different kind of imbalance through scale rather than number.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #128

stops.whyHere: Crossed gold vertical forms occupy the left eye zone; a tightly coiled spiral sits in the right. Finger-like projections along the upper edge blur where the head ends and something else begins.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W022's asymmetry is stark and immediate; W118 is more ambiguous — its two eye zones differ in structure, but the modeled dark volumes and lavender field make the split feel stranger and less resolved.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #125

chapters.title: Asymmetry Inside Dense Surfaces
chapters.introduction: These faces carry their asymmetry inside surfaces packed with layered lines and competing marks. The split between the eyes is one visible difference among many.

stops.whyHere: One eye recedes into shadow with a small orange ring; the other opens onto a red starburst. Dense scribble lines across the whole surface hold the two sides inside a single pressurized form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W118's dark volumes feel sculptural and contained; W040 is equally dense but more agitated, its scribbled surface making the eye asymmetry feel like one symptom of a broader restlessness.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #95

stops.whyHere: Two ring-eyes share the same concentric structure but sit at different heights and sizes, giving the squat brown mass an off-balance stare. Layers of colored lines fill every gap between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W040's two eyes differ in kind — shadow versus starburst; W063's eyes share a structure but differ in placement and scale, a subtler split inside an equally dense surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #36

stops.whyHere: A square eye crossed with orange diagonals faces a plain circle, both leaving white voids at center. Orange strokes push upward between them while looping lines extend past the face into the dark border.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W063's ring-eyes are contained within the face mass; W068's lines escape the boundary entirely, making the asymmetry feel less held-in and more volatile.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #109

chapters.title: Split to the Edge
chapters.introduction: The final group pushes asymmetry toward its limit: faces where competing mark systems or a single overwhelming feature make the two sides feel like separate compositions sharing one outline.

stops.whyHere: A concentric spiral eye on the left and a cross-hatched rectangular zone on the right sit inside a head packed with competing lines. The red-framed mouth and zigzag crown keep the split from resolving.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W068's lines escape the face edge; W006 contains its line noise within the head but packs it so tightly the two eye zones feel like separate systems forced into one form.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #18

stops.whyHere: One enormous black-and-white spiral eye consumes the upper center while the left side holds a yellow-outlined rectangle with a bold magenta stroke — the face has reorganized itself around a single overwhelming feature.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W006 distributes its competing systems across the whole head; W125 collapses that tension into one dominant eye, leaving the rest of the face to fill in around it in flat zones of yellow, magenta, and sky blue.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #79

nifty-faces--silhouette-and-shadow.scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W026 (nifty faces #62): The image shows a realistic, softly rendered face with warm amber tones and visible eyes — the draft description of 'web of quick black lines' and 'pale circular shapes' overstates the mark-making character visible at this resolution. The face is more tonally painted than line-built. Corrected to reflect visible tonal rendering and the green-accented eye.

W092 (nifty faces #60): The larger anchor image confirms the background is largely white/pale, not a 'grey and brown tonal block' as described. Crimson brushstrokes frame and invade the composition on a white ground. The draft's description of 'grey and brown tonal blocks' is inaccurate. Corrected to pale/white ground with grey-brown central form.

W092 transition from W065: Draft says 'W065's sparse white lines on black gave the face room to breathe; W092 fills every plane with crossing colour, replacing emptiness with relentless accumulation.' This is accurate and supported by both images. Retained.

W004 (nifty faces #94): The larger anchor image confirms the form is a heavily outlined, panel-like dark mass on warm brown — not a 'rounded form' in the soft sense. The fanned white lines at lower left and scribbled colour at crown are confirmed. The draft description is broadly accurate. Minor language tightening applied.

W088 (nifty faces #66): The image shows a large dark head in three-quarter view on a pale grey-white ground, with warm amber/orange breaking through. The draft description is accurate. The transition from W004 ('armour-like panels give the dark form a hard edge; W088's dark mass has no such boundary') is visually supported.

W092 chapter placement: W092 is placed in 'Noise and Pressure' but its white ground makes it visually distinct from W004 and W088 which have warm/dark grounds. However, the density of mark-making is the shared quality, which is the chapter's stated logic. Placement is defensible.

W104 (nifty faces #28): The image confirms a tilted rectangular block on dark teal with dense hatching and white marks. The draft's closing role as 'honest outlier' is appropriate. The transition from W126 referencing 'surrounding darkness of the teal ground' is visually supported.

W124 (nifty faces #100): The image confirms diagonal bands of teal and dark red-brown, looping outlines, and a cluster of brighter colours at the upper face. The draft description is accurate. The spiral at the cheek is visible.

W122 (nifty faces #56): The image confirms a skull-like form with dark eye sockets, a jaw area with vertical lines, and orange looping outlines on a warm amber-yellow ground. The draft description is accurate.
W105 (nifty faces #72): The image confirms white skull-like patches on black with red marks in the eye sockets and a tooth row. The draft description is accurate.
W065 (nifty faces #71): The image confirms a long dark face inside a hair-arch on grey ground with white lines for features. The draft description is accurate.
W039 (nifty faces #104): The image confirms a head in profile/three-quarter view with white lines, red-orange marks, and a dark blue-black ground on the left. The draft description is accurate.
W084 (nifty faces #103): The image confirms dark washes across the face with orange structural lines and a pale grey background. The draft description is accurate.
W093 (nifty faces #69): The image confirms olive-yellow face tones, black eye sockets, white scribble lines, and a geometric net at the bottom. The draft description is accurate.
W046 (nifty faces #58): The image confirms layered lines, dark-red eye hollows, and translucent circles. The draft description is accurate.
W101 (nifty faces #61): The image confirms overlapping pale circles in the background, looping lines for facial features, and blue irises. The draft description is accurate.

W126 (nifty faces #38): The larger anchor image confirms blue scribble-work on the upper dome, two yellow-gold bars in near-black eye sockets, and small white teeth at lower right with multicolour scribbles around the mouth. The draft description is accurate.
Chapter 1 transition for W101: Draft says 'Where W026 uses a dark surround to press the face forward, here the background glows softly' — this is visually supported by both images.

Chapter 4 W058 placement: W058 is placed as a contrast within the skull chapter, which is justified by its tooth row and structural vocabulary, though it is more colourful and outward-pressing than the other two. The draft acknowledges this contrast explicitly, which is appropriate.

Corrected W026 prose to reflect tonal painting rather than line-built surface. Corrected W092 ground description from 'grey and brown tonal blocks' to reflect pale/white ground with grey-brown central form.
evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change
evidence.assistantWordingScope: Specificity and overstatement corrections to exhibition headings and invitations. Existing image-reviewed memberships, chapter order and artwork roles remain intact.

nifty-faces--silhouette-and-shadow.title: Dark Mass, Small Light
nifty-faces--silhouette-and-shadow.question: How little light does a face need to remain a face?
nifty-faces--silhouette-and-shadow.introduction: Sixteen works each test the same question from a different position. Some faces are still largely readable, their surfaces layered but their features present. Others retreat behind dark washes, dense mark-making, or near-total blackness, holding on by a single bright accent — a yellow bar, a tooth row, a blue iris. The exhibition traces that gradual withdrawal and asks where recognition ends.
nifty-faces--silhouette-and-shadow.closing: By the final works, the question is no longer whether a face is present but whether the small remaining light is enough to hold it together — and what kind of light counts.

chapters.title: Surface and Presence
chapters.introduction: Four faces where the form is still largely readable, but the surface already resists easy description — layered with marks or tonal depth that complicate what lies beneath.

stops.whyHere: Warm amber tones and soft tonal rendering keep the face legible while the near-black background begins the gallery's slow withdrawal of light.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #62

stops.whyHere: Soft overlapping circles dissolve the background into pale gold; two blue irises hold steady as the only cool, fixed points in a warm haze.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous face is pressed forward by a dark surround, here the background glows softly, yet the downward tilt creates a similar sense of guarded distance.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #61

stops.whyHere: Dense overlapping lines replace tonal modelling; dark-red eye hollows pull inward while translucent circles push the surrounding space outward simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The blue irises of the previous work gave a clear focal point; here the eye positions are voids, and attention scatters across the layered surface instead.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #58

stops.whyHere: Muted teal and rust diagonal bands hold the face in place; a burst of gold and blue at the crown is the one point where the image releases pressure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's muted lavender-grey palette gives way to teal and rust bands, but both share a compressed, downward-cast quality that withholds direct engagement.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #100

chapters.title: Line Against Dark
chapters.introduction: Four works where darkness has claimed most of the surface and drawn lines — rather than tonal gradation — carry the work of keeping a face present.

stops.whyHere: Horizontal dark-blue-grey washes cover most of the face; orange lines trace structure without filling it, leaving the form open to the pale ground behind.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's diagonal bands were muted but still colourful; here the wash is heavier and cooler, and the face begins to recede rather than hold its ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #103

stops.whyHere: White lines cross cheekbone and jaw while cool blue and warm red fields pull against each other; the face tilts downward into shadow at its lower edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use line to describe structure over a dark field, but here competing warm and cool grounds create a tension the previous work's quieter palette avoids.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #104

stops.whyHere: Black eye sockets read as pure absence; white scribble lines layer over olive-grey skin like static, while a rigid geometric net below presses against the softness above.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's unresolved edges dissolve into ground; here a hard diagrammatic shape at the bottom makes the collision between two visual systems explicit.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #69

stops.whyHere: A long black face hangs inside a heavy arch of hair-like loops; white lines pick out drooping eyes and four elongated teeth, leaving most of the interior empty.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's geometric net imposed an external system on the face; here the surrounding arch is organic but equally enclosing, and the interior is even more stripped back.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #71

chapters.title: Buried Under Marks
chapters.introduction: Three works where the face is covered by dense, competing mark-making. The question of recognition shifts from shadow to sheer visual accumulation.

stops.whyHere: Crimson borders press inward on a pale ground while yellow-green and blue threads pull outward; two red rectangles act as anchors inside a surface of continuous agitation.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's sparse white lines on black gave the face room to breathe; here every plane is filled with crossing colour, replacing emptiness with relentless accumulation.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #60

stops.whyHere: Black-outlined panels lock together across a dark mass; fanned white lines at the lower left and scribbled colour at the crown create tension between containment and exposure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work spreads its marks across an open pale ground; here the same density is compressed into a sealed dark form on warm brown, making the pressure feel structural rather than scattered.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #94

stops.whyHere: A dark mass fills the frame; red, orange, and yellow-green lines gather thickest at brow and mouth, reading as friction rather than description of features.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's outlined panels give the dark form a hard edge; here the dark mass has no such boundary — warm lines push back against it from within, with no clear resolution.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #66

chapters.title: Skull Logic
chapters.introduction: Three works that strip the face back to its most reduced vocabulary — sockets, teeth, and outline — testing how little structural information recognition actually requires.

stops.whyHere: Eye sockets are dark holes; the jaw is a cage of vertical lines on a warm amber ground; orange outlines overshoot the form rather than containing it, giving the structure a restless quality.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's dark mass was built up from layered marks; here density is stripped away, leaving only outline and void — the face as hollow architecture.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #56

stops.whyHere: White patches assemble a skull-like face against pure black; repeated tooth loops make the grin feel insistent rather than fixed, holding the image between confrontation and dark comedy.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's skull sits on a warm amber ground with looping orange lines; here all warmth is removed — black ground, white patches only — making the reduction absolute.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #72

stops.whyHere: The face pushes outward rather than receding: white cross marks and a bold tooth row hold the eye at the surface, a structural contrast to the preceding skull works.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works foreground teeth as a primary feature, but where the previous work recedes into black, here layered colour and asymmetric eye zones press the face forward.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #52

chapters.title: The Last Light
chapters.introduction: Two works where darkness has absorbed most of the form and a single small accent — yellow bars, white marks — is all that remains to locate the face.

stops.whyHere: Blue scribble-work covers the upper dome; two yellow-gold bars in near-black eye sockets and small white teeth below are the only warm light in a cold, shadowed mass.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face pushed outward with dense colour; here darkness claims the bulk of the form and only two small yellow bars remain as evidence of a face.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #38

stops.whyHere: A tilted block floats in open teal space; a white spiral-and-cross and a cluster of white vertical bars are the only clear focal points inside dense hatching — an honest outlier that tests the gallery's question from a non-figurative angle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work holds recognition through two yellow bars in deep shadow; here white marks inside dense line-work serve a similar anchoring role, while the teal ground echoes the same question of how little is enough.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #28

nifty-faces--bared-teeth.scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W132 (nifty faces #8): The larger anchor image shows the eyes are NOT closed — they are open, with visible brow lines and eye marks. The draft claim 'closed eyes above refuse to confirm the sound below' is factually wrong and must be removed. The eyes read as narrowed or squinting under dense crosshatching, but they are not shut. Corrected to reflect open but heavily marked eyes.
W132 transition from W108: The draft says 'W132's are shut under dense crosshatching' — this is incorrect per the anchor image. Eyes are open/narrowed. Transition rewritten to avoid this false claim.

W053 (nifty faces #130): The anchor image confirms the mouth is a compressed, partially open oval with small visible teeth — not a wide-brimmed hat with a 'compressed dark oval' as the observation states. The hat is wide-brimmed and the face is bulbous and floats on lime green. The draft reading is broadly consistent but the 'compressed mouth' description is accurate. No major correction needed beyond confirming the hat is visible and the face floats in open ground.

W050 (nifty faces xmas special): Observations are thin ('pale cap', 'broad moustache', 'fine purple, cyan and white lines'). The image at sheet resolution shows a close portrait with a pale/white cap, visible moustache, bared teeth, and layered translucent colors on a dark ground. The draft reading is consistent with visible evidence. No invented details found.

W002: The anchor image confirms radiating purple eyes (left larger), diagonal pale beams, and a rectangular tooth row. The draft closing role ('compresses everything inward') is supported. No correction needed.

Chapter 1 (W132 stop): 'closed eyes' claim removed and rewritten. The eyes in W132 are open but heavily marked with dense crosshatching above; the open mouth below is the dominant feature. The transition from W108 is rewritten accordingly.

W027: Observations describe 'parted mouth revealing a row of small, tightly packed teeth' and 'no deep dark opening visible behind the teeth.' The image at sheet resolution is consistent with this. Draft placement in Volume and Shadow chapter is appropriate.

W064: The draft describes 'stacked tooth bands read as both grin and grid' and 'dense crosshatched strokes in lime, teal, red, and yellow.' The sheet image confirms a blocky rectangular head with stacked horizontal tooth bands and dense colored hatching. Consistent.
W087: 'One eye stares from a deep socket while the other sits empty' — confirmed by sheet image showing asymmetric eye sockets. Consistent.
W110: Draft says 'identical flat eyes suggest a mask worn' — sheet image confirms two eye sockets with identical red-mark-on-white construction. Consistent.

No unsupported artist psychology, chronology, or influence claims found in the draft. No invented objects beyond the W132 eye error. Repetitive language check: 'flat ground' and 'push toward the viewer' appear multiple times but in different specific contexts; acceptable. 'Mask-like' appears in multiple chapters — reduced where possible in revision.
Chapter pacing: Opening (readable) → Flat grounds → Surface pressure → Volume/shadow → Unresolved is a sound arc. No reordering needed.

nifty-faces--bared-teeth.title: Teeth Showing
nifty-faces--bared-teeth.question: What does the surrounding surface do to a mouth that is already open?
nifty-faces--bared-teeth.introduction: Twenty-five faces, each with teeth showing. Some sit against flat saturated grounds that push them forward; others dissolve into scribble or shadow. The exhibition follows the tooth-filled mouth from its most readable forms — where a first response is still available — through works where the marks covering the face pull so hard against the opening that no single reading holds.
nifty-faces--bared-teeth.closing: Each face here shows its teeth. Whether that reads as greeting, warning, or something with no ready name depends on marks the works themselves leave unresolved.

chapters.title: A Legible First Reading
chapters.introduction: Four faces where the open mouth and its surroundings still allow a recognizable first response — before the surrounding marks begin to complicate it.

stops.whyHere: Looping lines and two saturated orange marks at the open mouth read as a gasp or cry, the clearest single emotional signal in the gallery.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #65

stops.whyHere: Yellow-green ground and raw open mouth share W005's forward pressure, but dense lash lines and layered skin tones add a held, watchful quality.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both faces push toward the viewer on vivid grounds; W045 replaces loose loops with dense layered flesh tones, making the open mouth feel more bodily.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #87

stops.whyHere: Teeth bared and eyes fixed forward, held inside a single white boundary line against plain brown silence — the most direct frontal address so far.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W045's face dissolves at the hair edges; W108 is sharply bounded by a white outline, making the same forward pressure feel contained and deliberate.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #47

stops.whyHere: The wide-open mouth dominates the lower half while concentric framing bands press the head toward the viewer; heavily marked eyes above narrow the face without confirming what the open jaw below is doing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W108's eyes are fixed and fully open; W132's are narrowed under dense crosshatching, so the open mouth below is the dominant readable feature but loses its confirming witness.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #8

chapters.title: Flat Grounds, Emblem Faces
chapters.introduction: Six works where a saturated, unmodulated background removes spatial depth, turning the face into something closer to a sign or emblem than a portrait.

stops.whyHere: Flat red-orange field, rectangular eye sockets, and bared teeth with smeared cheek strokes hold the face between fixed emblem and agitated surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W132's concentric bands frame a recognisable head; W007's flat red-orange ground removes all depth, pushing the face into emblem territory.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #77

stops.whyHere: Yellow ground, blank oval eyes, and a hard red crossbar divide the face into horizontal zones — rigid structure against restless looping surface lines.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W007's red field is warm and advancing; W012 switches to yellow with a dark head, reversing the figure-ground relationship while keeping the same flat spatial logic.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #99

stops.whyHere: Two full rows of teeth, crossed and striped eyes, and dense colored lines covering every surface make this the most overtly sign-like face in the chapter.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W012's face has one tooth row and some open ground; W015 doubles the teeth and fills every surface with line, intensifying the flat, frontal quality.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #42

stops.whyHere: Flower-burst eyes and hot-pink patches give the face an unsettled brightness; scribble lines sit visibly on top of the face structure rather than building it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W015's dense lines are packed and uniform; W021's scribble floats above the face structure, loosening the emblem into something more provisional.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #1

stops.whyHere: Magenta ground, mismatched eye forms — one gridded, one radial — and bared teeth hold confrontation and unease in the same flat space.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W021's eyes are symmetrical flower bursts; W072's two eye zones refuse to match at all, fracturing the face's symmetry on the same kind of flat ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #91

stops.whyHere: Wide flat-fronted head on a red ground, spiral eyes, and an open jaw with blocky teeth — the head fills the frame edge to edge, leaving almost no ground visible.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W072's magenta field leaves breathing room around the head; W078 returns to red and the head expands to fill nearly the entire frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #45

chapters.title: Surface Working Against the Mouth
chapters.introduction: Six faces where the marks covering the skin create a visual argument of their own — the tooth-filled mouth competes with a surface that appears to be doing something else.

stops.whyHere: Spiral-coil eyes and a rectangular open mouth read as shock, but layered color patches beneath the white outline fracture form and feeling simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W078's surface lines are loose and casual at the edges; W009's spiral eyes and dense color patches make the surface feel pressurised from within.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #55

stops.whyHere: Gold scribble fills the upper skull while solid black anchors the shoulders; bared teeth and green irises sit between warm chaos above and cool weight below.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W009's pressure is distributed across the whole face; W024 splits the figure — warm scribble above, solid black below — giving the tension a clear vertical axis.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #86

stops.whyHere: White scribble lines pile across broad color patches, flattening depth even as goggle eyes and bared teeth push toward alarm or exaggeration.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W024's split is vertical; W030's white scribble covers the entire surface uniformly, dissolving the axis while keeping the same forward pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #64

stops.whyHere: Dense overlapping lines pack the face until it reads as a container; identical flat eyes suggest a worn surface, while the tooth-filled mouth stays warm and loud.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W030's scribble is white on color; W110's lines are multicolored and leave no gap, making the face feel more saturated and less readable as volume.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #81

stops.whyHere: Dense crosshatched strokes in lime, teal, red, and yellow pack every surface, yet thick black outlines hold the geometry firm; stacked tooth bands read as both grin and grid.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W110's outlines are loose green loops; W064's thick black geometry reasserts firm structure against the same dense interior line-work.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #27

stops.whyHere: Tooth-filled mouth and spiky gold brow forms pull against each other; dense black hatching builds weight at the core while cyan and pink lines escape beyond the head's boundary.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W064's lines are packed inside firm outlines; W130's lines escape beyond the head's edge, suggesting pressure finding its limits rather than being contained.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #110

chapters.title: Volume and Shadow
chapters.introduction: Five faces that use modeled light and shadow rather than flat grounds, giving the teeth a different kind of weight — embedded in mass rather than announced against color.

stops.whyHere: Deep shadow on one side and a bleached highlight on the other build a solid rounded volume; colored scribble sits across the modelled surface like static.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W130's marks escape outward on a flat ground; W027 introduces genuine modelled volume, so the scribble lines read as surface noise on a solid form.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #124

chapters.title: The Expression That Will Not Settle
chapters.introduction: Four faces where the open mouth and the surrounding marks pull in opposite directions, leaving the expression without a stable reading.

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W053's face is wary and compressed; W077's angular geometry inside soft scribble introduces a more active internal conflict between structure and surface.

stops.whyHere: Lopsided eyes give an off-balance stare; the red-orange lip line is the only warm accent in a cool dark field, pulling the eye to the wide tooth-filled mouth.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W077's conflict is between geometry and scribble; W114's conflict is between a cool dark ground and the single warm red-orange lip line, making the mouth the only resolved point.

nifty-faces--objects-letters-emblems.title: When the Face Carries Signs
nifty-faces--objects-letters-emblems.question: What can a face still communicate once its features have been replaced, interrupted, or overwritten by marks and objects?
nifty-faces--objects-letters-emblems.introduction: These twenty-five works share a single territory: the human face as a surface where marks, symbols, and objects compete with portraiture. Some faces carry their signs lightly; others are nearly consumed by them. Moving from crossed eyes and barred mouths through gridded diagrams and split color fields, the exhibition traces how far a sign can advance into a face before the portrait disappears.
nifty-faces--objects-letters-emblems.closing: Each work leaves the question open differently. Whether a sign cancels a feature or simply joins it, something shifts in what the face can hold and what it can no longer show.

chapters.title: The X and the Eye
chapters.introduction: Four faces where a single repeated mark — the X or cross — lands directly on the eyes, converting the gaze into a sign of blockage or negation.

stops.whyHere: Two large green irises each carry a bold red X; the mark dominates both eye zones and sets the exhibition's central question immediately.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #93

stops.whyHere: Flat black silhouette against pink; yellow X shapes inside rigid rectangular eye frames echo the crossed eyes but flatten them into pure graphic marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous X marks sit inside spiraling organic irises, here they occupy hard-edged rectangles — the same sign, stripped of any biological surround.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #82

stops.whyHere: One eye burns red through a lattice of crossing lines; the other sits dim and closed, making the blockage uneven rather than absolute.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face applied identical X marks to both eyes symmetrically; here the crossing belongs to only one socket, introducing imbalance where the earlier face was evenly sealed.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #116

stops.whyHere: Dense crossed black lines fill both oval eye forms inside a loose white-line face; the marks read as sealed, the whole structure dissolving into dark ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous asymmetric lattice eye still held a recognizable face; here the crossed eyes dissolve into a muted brown field, the face barely holding together around them.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #59

chapters.title: Objects in Place of Features
chapters.introduction: Works where a discrete object — a hand, a heart, glasses — occupies the position of a facial feature, displacing rather than decorating it.

stops.whyHere: A pale hand pressed outward covers the entire eye zone; only teeth remain visible below, making concealment itself the dominant feature.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous crossed marks sealed the eyes with line; here the eye zone is replaced entirely by a physical object, making the absence of gaze literal and frontal.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #74

stops.whyHere: A dark-red heart with crossed yellow bars sits where eyes would be, above bared teeth — an affectionate shape complicated by the crossing marks above it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work used a hand to block the gaze; here a heart substitutes — a different kind of object, one that carries its own symbolic weight before the crossing marks complicate it.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #108

stops.whyHere: Rectangular glasses ride at two different heights across the face — one lens on the forehead, one near the eye — present but visibly displaced from their function.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work placed a symbolic object in the eye zone; here the correct object for that zone appears but sits askew, so the displacement is one of position rather than kind.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #131

stops.whyHere: Eyeglass frames form the one steady horizontal in an otherwise restless surface, anchoring the face while everything above and below breaks into competing marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous glasses were slipping; these frames hold firm as the composition's single geometric anchor, making the object feel load-bearing rather than decorative.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #2

stops.whyHere: A flat-brimmed hat and oversized rectangular lenses compress the face into stacked zones, two objects framing the head from top to bottom.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous glasses anchored a restless face; here a hat above them means two objects now define the face from crown to jaw, leaving little room for features between.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #85

chapters.title: Marks That Contest the Portrait
chapters.introduction: Faces where geometric signs, scribbled lines, or color divisions actively compete with the portrait for visual authority — neither fully winning.

stops.whyHere: The face splits into warm red-brown and cool teal halves; looping pink crossed-oval eye marks and a dot row across the forehead divide the surface into competing systems.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous objects sat on top of a coherent face; here the face itself divides into two color fields, so the split is structural rather than applied.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #115

stops.whyHere: Broad orange and cyan bands pass across the head, partially obscuring crossed yellow eye forms; portrait and horizontal color field compete across the same surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous split ran vertically down the center; here bands cross horizontally, a different axis of interruption over a face that remains more naturalistically rendered.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #114

stops.whyHere: Stacked rectangular zones — hat, brow, eyes, mouth — each packed with crossing lines in lime, magenta, and red; the face becomes a column of pressurized compartments.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous bands interrupted a recognizable head; here the face is rebuilt entirely from stacked rectangular zones, so the compartmentalization is now the structure, not an overlay.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #17

stops.whyHere: Stripes, zigzag bands, spiral eyes, and a V-mouth stack in rows; the face is a flat grid of repeating marks rather than a modeled form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous zones were densely packed but still face-shaped; here the image flattens further into a striped grid where every zone carries the same visual weight.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #26

stops.whyHere: Two spiral-filled squares pull the eye inward while slashing straight lines cut through them at steep angles; the face is a site of competing directional energies.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous marks ran in orderly rows; here slashing diagonal lines break that regularity, introducing force that cuts across the face's organizing structure.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #32

stops.whyHere: Saturated purple swallows the head's outline; yellow eye zones and a gridded jaw frame the face as something between a mask and a diagram, contained but restless.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous energy was centrifugal, lines escaping outward; here everything is pulled inward against a flat purple field, the face compressed rather than dispersed.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #121

stops.whyHere: Hard-edged rectangles lock the eye zones while loose scattered strokes overflow the face boundary; a downward triangle anchors the lower half with green zigzag marks inside.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face was compressed by its ground; here the rigid frames are surrounded by lines that refuse to stay inside the figure's edges, the face pushing back outward.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #6

chapters.title: Letters, Numbers, and Diagrams
chapters.introduction: Works where legible text, repeated symbols, or diagrammatic layouts enter the face, making the image readable as both portrait and notation simultaneously.

stops.whyHere: Bubble-outlined letters NN, XYZ fill two framed rectangles; a plus-in-circle and a row of oval loops complete a face-shaped schematic built from text and symbols.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face was built from geometric frames; here equivalent frames are filled with actual letters and a plus sign, making the schematic explicitly linguistic.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #48

stops.whyHere: Three framed squares each hold a red X over a yellow circle — one more than a face typically carries — giving the structure a serial, mechanical quality.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous letter blocks were unique marks; here the same framed symbol repeats three times in a row, introducing seriality that pushes the image toward diagram rather than portrait.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #92

stops.whyHere: Identical lobed wheel eyes sit like dials on a teal ground; chained orange ovals, a bar of yellow blocks, and a dangling frame make the face read as something mounted or broadcast.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous repeated X-circles were hand-drawn and rough; here the lobed wheels and chained ovals feel more mechanical, the face assembled from components rather than drawn.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #123

stops.whyHere: Packed ladders, triangles, small head-like forms, and a red heart-like shape resist a single facial reading; the image oscillates between a possible face and a field of separate signs.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous components were spatially organized around a face structure; here the sign field densifies until the face becomes one possible reading among many competing ones.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #0000

chapters.title: The Face Reduced to Structure
chapters.introduction: Five works where the sign system has advanced so far that the face is present only in placement or outline — the features no longer dominant, the signs no longer decorative.

stops.whyHere: A heavy mask against wavy orange stripes; red spirals, a bead row, and blunt white teeth give the face a ceremonial weight where ornament and structure are inseparable.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous signs competed with a possible face; here the face has become fully ceremonial, its features indistinguishable from the decorative system surrounding them.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #126

stops.whyHere: An orange-red arc, a bisecting vertical, an X, and a looping circle occupy the face zone; the composition resists settling into a fixed boundary or a readable portrait.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous mask was heavy and frontal; here the face disperses into floating marks against a dark field, the portrait dissolving into its component signs.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #50

stops.whyHere: Three dripping columns dominate the frame; small red marks at the edges are the only face-like accents in an image where columnar forms have displaced any portrait structure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous image still held a face-shaped zone at center; here columnar forms replace it, and facial features survive only as marginal red marks at the edges.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #83

stops.whyHere: A hooded purple form carries two white rectangular blocks — eyes and teeth — as flat mask segments; a yellow dot chain and spiky marks at one eye are the only signs of life in the dark mass.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face marks were marginal and small; here the face returns to center but as a mask of two flat white blocks, the portrait reduced to its minimum legible components.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #73

stops.whyHere: Circular glasses anchor a frontal face while scribbled lines radiate outward beyond the head's outline in all directions; the face holds center as the sign system escapes around it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face was absorbed into darkness; here a frontal presence reasserts itself, but the radiating lines suggest the face is actively losing its boundary to the marks surrounding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #4

nifty-faces--accumulation-and-dissolutio.title: Faces Made of Layers
nifty-faces--accumulation-and-dissolutio.question: At what point does the accumulation of marks stop describing a face and become its own subject?
nifty-faces--accumulation-and-dissolutio.introduction: These twenty-one works share a single subject — the human face — but treat it as a site where marks multiply, compete, and sometimes overwhelm what they describe. Moving from portraits where features hold their ground through works where mark systems run on their own logic, the exhibition asks how much a face can absorb before the marks become the primary event.
nifty-faces--accumulation-and-dissolutio.closing: Each work here began with a face. Whether it still ends with one — or with something the marks have replaced — is a question each visitor will reach at a different point.

chapters.title: The Face Holds
chapters.introduction: Three works where recognizable features — eyes, nose, mouth — remain legible despite visible layering. The marks are present but the face is still the dominant reading.

stops.whyHere: Thick black outlines hold the face against a dark ground with warm amber and gold tones in the face area; scattered blue scribbles float above without dissolving the form.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #105

stops.whyHere: Dense color marks crowd every surface, yet small dark pupils and a tight mouth keep pulling the portrait back into focus.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W014 uses bold outlines to hold the face, W017 relies on two steady pupils inside a storm of orange and cyan strokes.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #41

stops.whyHere: A dense horizontal band of crossing lines forms the hat brim above a face built from the same layered scribble technique, keeping the portrait legible under accumulated pressure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W017's face is held by color contrast; W054 adds a structural horizontal anchor above a face equally dense but more tightly compressed around recognizable features.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #11

chapters.title: Structure Under Strain
chapters.introduction: Works where the face is still present but its features have been reorganized into competing systems — spirals, grids, slashes — each running on its own visual logic.

stops.whyHere: A face assembled from circular arcs alone, without an enclosing outline — the minimum marks needed for recognition, nothing more.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W054 is dense with layered marks yet fully legible; W047 offers the opposite extreme, showing how few marks a face actually requires.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #113

stops.whyHere: A tilted oval head crossed by dense colored lines; the tilt and the red-rimmed mouth keep the face readable inside its own tangle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W047's face floats in open gray space; W049 fills the same oval territory with crossing lines that crowd but do not erase the features.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #34

stops.whyHere: Asymmetric eyes and a dark mass against teal hold the face together while loose surface lines work against that stillness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W049's lines cross a tilted head in motion; W055 is heavy and still, the asymmetric eyes introducing an off-balance quality that replaces agitation with unease.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #129

stops.whyHere: Spiral eyes pull inward while crossing lines push outward; a purple triangle lodged in one eye introduces a geometric note that unsettles the symmetry.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W055's face is dark and compressed; W082 opens into warm red, but competing spiral and geometric systems create a different kind of internal pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #33

stops.whyHere: Three separate mark systems — spirals at the eyes, red arcs at the mouth, dense hatching between — occupy the same face without merging.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W082's asymmetry is subtle; W032 makes the collision of systems explicit, each zone running a visibly different logic against the burgundy ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #19

chapters.title: The Face as Architecture
chapters.introduction: Works where the face has been reorganized into stacked chambers, rectangular zones, or structural grids — still a face, but one that reads as built rather than drawn.

stops.whyHere: Stacked rectangular chambers each hold a separate color argument; the face reads as architecture, with a spiked crown pressing up and a scribble-filled band anchoring below.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W032's systems collide inside a recognizable face; W036 separates those systems into discrete chambers, giving the conflict a formal, architectural order.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #78

stops.whyHere: Spiral eyes and a yellow circle border impose strict symmetry; the rectangular mouth filled with vertical bars reads as locked or frozen mid-sound.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W036's chambers are irregular and pressured; W056 regularizes the same idea into near-perfect symmetry, which makes the locked mouth feel more deliberate.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #68

stops.whyHere: Two dark oval forms above a grid of vertical black lines give the face a blunt, mechanical quality; the teal field holds color blocks apart without resolving them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W056's symmetry is decorative and cool; W090 strips the same structural approach to its most blunt form — dark ovals over a packed vertical grid.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #75

stops.whyHere: Nested rectangles for eyes and vertical bars for a mouth push the face toward raw confrontation; a bold yellow wave outside the head keeps the composition from closing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W090's face is flat and mechanical; W100 adds dense crossing lines and a bold yellow stroke that sits outside the head, making the structure feel pressured rather than inert.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #67

stops.whyHere: Two paired black squares hold spirals above a wide dark band of white rectangles; bead strings extend outward along horizontal lines, blurring where the face ends.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W100's yellow wave escapes the head shape; W070 extends that outward drift further, with bead-like forms pulling the face's edges into the surrounding field.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #119

chapters.title: Marks Competing for the Same Space
chapters.introduction: Works where multiple mark systems — hatching, loops, spirals, slashes — press against each other until the face becomes a site of collision rather than a stable description.

stops.whyHere: Dense scribble covers a three-quarter head; a second face folded into the right edge makes the form feel watched from two directions at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W070's face blurs at its edges; W041 folds a second face into the same form, doubling the pressure without doubling the space.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #122

stops.whyHere: Two heads press together, teeth exposed, outlines tangled; the magenta ground pushes forward rather than receding, compressing the figures.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W041 folds two views of one head; W086 presses two distinct heads into the same space, their open mouths and tangled outlines making the collision explicit.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #111

stops.whyHere: Two coiled spirals pull the eye inward from opposite sides; dense crosshatching fills every gap, holding tension between stillness and overload.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W086's collision is between two figures; W069 concentrates the same intensity into a single face where two spiral eyes create a fixed, staring standoff.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #29

stops.whyHere: A flat-topped mass of dense hatching presses down over two small circles; the triple border contains the pressure without releasing it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W069's spirals pull inward; W059 reverses the force — a heavy mass presses downward over barely visible circles, the border holding everything tight.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #20

stops.whyHere: A roughly spherical form built entirely from crossing lines, with no solid fills; bright flare points read as pressure from within the structure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W059's mass presses down from above; W033 distributes that pressure evenly across a rounded form, so the force has no single direction.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #23

chapters.title: When the Marks Take Over
chapters.introduction: Works where the face is nominally present but the marks have become the primary event — features reduced to fixed points inside a field that operates on its own terms.

stops.whyHere: Dense looping lines build a face-like form that never fully settles; the eye-like ovals hold steady while the surrounding mass keeps shifting between hair, shadow, and pure mark.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W033's form is evenly pressured; W023 introduces a hierarchy — two dark ovals hold while everything around them refuses to resolve.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #22

stops.whyHere: The head holds together only through accumulated line pressure; two black cross marks stand in for eyes, giving the face a flat, locked quality on an open white ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W023's eye-like ovals are organic and shifting; W043 replaces them with blunt black crosses, making the face's dependence on placeholder marks visible.
stops.title: nnxyz nifty faces #21

stops.whyHere: A dense central knot of overlapping lines sits above a calm row of evenly spaced rectangles; the contrast between compressed tangle and measured row holds the image at the edge of release.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W043's marks are restless on white; W096 adds a sudden calm band below the tangle, making the pressure above feel more deliberate by contrast.
