scrimshaw--face-as-field.title: Scrimshaw: The Face as Field
scrimshaw--face-as-field.question: As marks accumulate across these works, at what point does a face become a pattern of strokes?
scrimshaw--face-as-field.introduction: Twenty-six works move from faces held together by a single dominant contour, through surfaces crowded with competing marks and asymmetric features, into doubled figures, grids, and crowds, and close with standing bodies and two large letters. At each stage, the same visible question recurs: how many marks can occupy a face before the face itself becomes secondary to the marks?
scrimshaw--face-as-field.closing: The two large letters at the end are built from the same layered strokes as the faces at the start. Whether they continue the portrait or replace it remains a question the works leave open.

chapters.title: One Contour Does the Work
chapters.introduction: Three works open with faces where a single dominant line—blue, purple, or warm orange—carries the structure, while softer marks occupy the space around or behind it.

stops.whyHere: A single heavy blue line carves the face; soft lavender and yellow circles behind it contrast with the jagged foreground, making the contour feel exposed rather than settled.
stops.title: Scrimshaw1

stops.whyHere: Purple arcs replace the blue contour; the head floats against open sky-blue with more bare ground visible, the boundary between figure and field already loosening.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use one dominant color to trace the head, but here far more empty ground surrounds the form, making the face feel less anchored.
stops.title: Scrimshaw4

stops.whyHere: A long face and narrow neck stand against purple; white loops mark features while an extra forehead oval complicates the usual facial map without overwhelming the contour.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous head floats freely against open ground, this narrow face is pulled downward by its long neck, trading openness for vertical tension.
stops.title: Scrimshaw8

chapters.title: No Single Line Governs
chapters.introduction: Seven works layer overlapping strokes across the face until color, asymmetry, and repetition share the surface equally, with no one mark settling the whole.

stops.whyHere: A spiral vortex reads as an eye socket while slashing cyan lines scatter attention outward; the salmon field contains the collision without resolving it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single governing contour of the previous chapter dissolves here into competing colored scribbles pressing against a warm, unbroken background.
stops.title: Scrimshaw9

stops.whyHere: Broad orange and pink masses give the tilted face volume while fine blue loops keep its edges unsettled against bright yellow.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a warm field to contain a tangled head, but this face tilts and its features stay open rather than pressurized.
stops.title: Scrimshaw6

stops.whyHere: Thick red, black, and yellow lines crowd a large head; differently framed eyes and rows of oval mouth-marks briefly steady an otherwise dense surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The warm-field looseness of the previous work tightens here: the head nearly fills the square and the marks grow heavier and more insistent.
stops.title: Scrimshaw6

stops.whyHere: Rectangular scaffolding in red and blue holds soft pink fills; orbiting purple and yellow loops extend past the head into the orange field, giving the face a constructed, pressurized quality.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a yellow-orange ground and crowded marks, but this head introduces rigid rectangular shapes that make the face feel built rather than drawn.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 18

stops.whyHere: Long strokes fan outward above the tilted head, carrying the face's restless energy into the surrounding yellow space beyond the skull's edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The orbiting loops of the previous work become directional here: marks escape upward and outward rather than circling the form.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 21

stops.whyHere: A white X over one eye area reads as cancellation; the open red mouth with crude teeth holds the mood between shout and grin against a flat gray field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bright yellow ground gives way to flat gray, isolating the figure more starkly and making the X-mark feel like a deliberate interruption rather than overflow.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 40

stops.whyHere: Three eye-like forms at different heights give the face an unsteady gaze; vertical bars across the mouth make the expression harder to settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single X-mark of the previous work expands here into three competing eye forms, multiplying the points of uncertainty across the face.
stops.title: Wobbler

chapters.title: Accumulation at Its Densest
chapters.introduction: Seven works push mark-making furthest, opening with one deliberate reduction before re-escalating. Spiral eyes, bared teeth, and radiating lines make the face a site of layered addition rather than a stable image.

stops.whyHere: A small elongated face sits within a wide spread of colored strands; the contrast between narrow head and expansive surroundings gives the portrait a different scale at each stage of looking.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After the crowded, nearly full-frame faces, this work pulls back: the head shrinks inside its own hair-like field, reversing the pressure before it builds again.
stops.title: Scrimshaw8

stops.whyHere: Mismatched spiral eyes and an open toothed mouth stare outward; a small secondary circle below the chin suggests the face is still accumulating downward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works show a face surrounded by tangled strands, but here the head reasserts its full-frame scale and the spiral eyes lock the gaze.
stops.title: Scrimshaw13

stops.whyHere: One eye is loose and layered, the other a tight bullseye; zigzag lines across the forehead and a gaping toothed mouth leave the expression unresolved against the bright yellow field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The spiral eyes of the previous work reappear here in a more extreme asymmetry, and the yellow ground intensifies the sense of forward pressure.
stops.title: Scrimshaw14

stops.whyHere: A pink-lavender spiral crown pulls the eye upward while bared teeth anchor below; a teal stripe splits the face into halves that do not mirror each other.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bullseye eye of the previous work becomes a full spiral crown here, and the face divides vertically rather than varying eye by eye.
stops.title: Scrimshaw7

stops.whyHere: Radiating hair-like strokes push outward in every direction; warm yellows and reds inside the face contrast with the cool blue ground at the corners.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The radiating lines that escaped upward in earlier works now push simultaneously in every direction, giving the head a sense of outward dispersal.
stops.title: Scrimshaw15

stops.whyHere: Layered loops construct a head that reads as both face and skull; chain-like forms at the bottom leave the figure's mood between restraint and ornament.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a hot yellow field and tangled reds, but this face introduces skull-like exposed teeth and chain forms that shift the register toward something more structural.
stops.title: Scrimshaw5

stops.whyHere: Three hollow spiral sockets stare with unsettling symmetry; warm golden tones seep through dense black scribble, giving the dark mass a faint glow that can read as either menacing or mournful.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The skull reading of the previous work intensifies here: the black ground and three symmetrical sockets make this the most mask-like and confrontational face in the sequence.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 41

chapters.title: One Face Becomes Several
chapters.introduction: Six works place more than one face in the same image—through split halves, paired profiles, three crowded heads, and a full grid—testing whether repetition clarifies or dissolves the subject.

stops.whyHere: A white X seals one eye while the other stays open; purple scribbles spill past the face into the background, dissolving the boundary between figure and field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The three-socket symmetry of the previous work breaks here: one side of the face is marked through, giving the two halves different weight.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 24

stops.whyHere: Layered neon outlines trace a skull in profile, each color pass slightly offset so the form appears to shift; a jagged crown reads as another restless loop rather than decoration.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The frontal face gives way to a profile, and the single-pass outline multiplies into layered offsets that make the skull appear to vibrate.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 42

stops.whyHere: Two hollow-looking heads face the same direction, packed with overlapping color tangles; a coral projection from the left head reaches into the gap without bridging the two forms.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single profile of the previous work doubles here, but the two heads remain isolated despite their closeness, the gap between them held open.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 33

stops.whyHere: Three black-outlined heads crowd the frame; white scrawl layered across their faces obscures mouths and eyes, lending the group a feeling of being partially erased.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two isolated profiles become three heads pressed shoulder to shoulder, and a new layer of white marks partially covers the features just established.
stops.title: Scrimshaw3

stops.whyHere: A roughly four-by-four grid boxes each face into its own cell; the purple ground pushes warmer fills forward so faces surface from noise, none fully winning attention.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three heads become a grid of many, the crowd formalized into cells where every face competes equally and no single one can hold the eye.
stops.title: Scrimshaw12

stops.whyHere: Dense overlapping loops form two mismatched hollow shapes; pale vertical lines drape across the surface, partially dissolving the face back into pattern.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The grid's many cells compress back into a single face, but vertical lines now dissolve it toward pure pattern, bridging the crowd and the figures that follow.
stops.title: Scrimshaw2

chapters.title: Figures and Letters Replace the Face
chapters.introduction: Three final works move away from the isolated portrait: figures stand in groups, and two large letters occupy the space where a single face appeared throughout.

stops.whyHere: Three narrow figures share an orange field; radiating side marks and a hovering oval above the central figure give the group a shared structure without merging it into one body.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The dissolving single face of the previous work gives way to three distinct upright figures, restoring bodily presence but distributing it across a group.
stops.title: Trio1

stops.whyHere: Five figures stand close together, thin lines crossing between them; loops above their heads repeat the same gesture across the group while uneven faces keep each figure distinct.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three figures become five, the crossing lines between bodies growing more insistent, togetherness and individuality held in the same tangled field.
stops.title: Stick Together

stops.whyHere: Two large letters built from layered colored strokes occupy the space where a face would be; the inner loops of the G echo the spiral eye forms seen throughout the exhibition.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The five standing figures give way to two letters that use the same overlapping mark language as every face in the show, asking whether the greeting replaces or simply is a face.
stops.title: GM

findings: W020 contains no identifiable human figure — the observations describe organic dome-like forms, dripping verticals, and a central glow, not a figure with a body. Its role as an 'edge-dissolving figure' was unsupported. Reassigned to an honest contrasting role as a field-only composition that sets up the silhouette chapter by contrast.

W258 is visibly a large skeletal/robotic figure that fills most of the frame against a black ground — it is not a small contained figure. The draft's closing chapter framed it as 'close and contained' which is accurate, but the claim that it 'holds its ground in deep black space' with a 'raised hand the only outward gesture' is supportable. However the draft described it as 'compact' when it visually dominates its frame. Corrected to 'fills the frame'.

W265 anchor image confirms the form is a snail (coiled shell with a small head and cross-marked eyes), not an abstract coiled form. The draft's 'cross-marked points read as weary or dazed' is an unsupported emotional claim about expression. Corrected to describe visible cross marks without claiming expression.

W237 anchor image confirms the background is open pastel washes (blue, pink, lavender) with blocky outlines at lower corners and a wire/line along the top — not 'soft color washes keep the ground open' which is accurate, but the draft also said 'the figure's reach claims the horizontal space' — this is supportable from the visible extended arm reaching to the disc at right. Retained with minor wording.

W250 is visibly an animal figure (bear or similar) inside a dark inner rectangle with bokeh-like light circles in the outer field — the draft called it a 'hunched figure' which is acceptable, but 'head down, limbs pulled inward' overstates posture detail at this resolution. Softened to what is visible: a dense figure within a dark frame, outer field glowing with soft circles.
The draft transition from W265 to W237 (chapter 3 opening) referenced W265's form as 'closed and still' versus W237's extended arm — this is visually supported and retained.
The draft chapter 2 transition from W020 to W106 described W020 as having 'crowded edges' — this is visible and supported. Retained.
W003 is correctly described: hat-dominated figure with dissolving pale circles. The 'face partly hidden beneath the hat's shadow' is visible. Supported.
W106 is correctly described: black dog silhouette lower right, vast blue field, yellow zigzag marks. Supported.
W220 is correctly described: small black silhouette, raised arm, yellow field, wavy lines from head. Supported.

Reordering: W020 moved to open Chapter 1 as a field-without-figure contrast, followed by W003 as the first figure whose edges dissolve — this creates a cleaner opening progression from pure field to dissolving figure. All 8 slots retained exactly once.
Removed stock phrase 'room to breathe' from chapter prose. Removed 'like sound made visible' metaphor from W106 description. Removed 'pressure or noise' unsupported reading from W265 whyHere.
W258 described as filling its frame rather than 'compact' to match visible image.

nnotb--open-fields.title: Figure and Ground
nnotb--open-fields.question: What does the space surrounding a figure do to its edges and its weight?
nnotb--open-fields.introduction: Eight works place figures — human, animal, skeletal, snail — inside fields that dissolve, dwarf, or press against them. Some figures lose their edges to overlapping washes; others hold a hard silhouette against a single open color. Moving through the gallery, notice how the surrounding ground shifts from active to empty, from glowing to dark.
nnotb--open-fields.closing: Each work leaves a different amount of room around its figure. Whether that room reads as exposure, compression, or openness depends on what the figure's own edges are doing.

chapters.title: Where the Figure Begins
chapters.introduction: The exhibition opens with a work offering almost no figure — only a field of organic forms and a lit center — before introducing a figure whose edges actively dissolve into its ground.

stops.whyHere: Rounded forms press in from all edges while a pale center holds open; there is no stable figure here, only a field in tension with itself — establishing the question of where a figure ends and its ground begins.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #20

stops.whyHere: A hat-and-face emerge from overlapping pale circles; the figure is present but its outline trades places with the background, answering W020's field-only tension by introducing a figure that cannot fully separate from its ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W020 offers only a crowded field with a lit center and no clear figure, W003 introduces a figure — but one whose edges dissolve into the same kind of diffuse, overlapping forms.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #115

chapters.title: Silhouette Against Open Color
chapters.introduction: Three works strip the figure to a flat black shape set against a single saturated ground, showing how much a solid form can hold when surrounded by unbroken color.

stops.whyHere: A black dog silhouette stands in the lower-right corner of a vast blue field; yellow zigzag marks radiate from it, the only marks of energy in an otherwise empty expanse.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After W003's dissolved edges, W106 moves to the opposite extreme — a hard black silhouette with no ambiguity at its border, set against a flat blue field that offers it almost no company.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #212

stops.whyHere: A small black figure raises one arm in a yellow field that fills the entire canvas; wavy lines fan from its head, but the yellow above remains unbroken and vast.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both W106 and W220 use a flat black silhouette against a single saturated ground, but W220 centers its figure lower and surrounds it with even more uninterrupted field above.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #130

stops.whyHere: A black snail form rests on a black ground strip; mixed straight and zigzag lines burst from behind its shell into yellow, yet the large empty upper field above makes the radiating marks feel small against the surrounding space.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W220's figure reaches upward into open yellow; W265's snail form turns inward, its shell enclosing a spiral while the same yellow field above remains unbroken and dominant.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #101

chapters.title: Figures That Reach Outward
chapters.introduction: Two works show figures extending into the picture plane — one gripping an object across open ground, one whose dense marks fill a framed interior while light drifts outside it.

stops.whyHere: A standing figure extends one arm across the composition to grip a tangle of lines leading to a glowing red disc; the open pastel washes behind it keep the ground light, making the figure's horizontal reach the dominant spatial event.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W265's snail is closed and low, W237's figure stands upright and extends an arm across the width of the image, actively measuring the space around it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #146

stops.whyHere: A dense figure sits inside a dark inner rectangle while soft light circles drift across the warm outer field; the visible frame within the image divides the surrounding space into an inner zone of dense marks and an outer zone of diffuse glow.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W237's figure stands in open, undivided space; W250 introduces a literal frame within the image, splitting the field into a dark interior and a glowing exterior.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #97

chapters.title: Figure Against Darkness
chapters.introduction: The final work removes the open field almost entirely, placing a figure against near-total black so that its own surface becomes the only available light.

stops.whyHere: A large skeletal figure fills the frame against deep black; white and orange lines trace its limbs and skull from within, so the figure carries its own light rather than drawing it from any surrounding field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W250's figure sits inside a dark rectangle with a glowing field visible beyond it; W258 removes that outer glow entirely, leaving the figure surrounded by black with only its own traced edges providing light.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #26

nnotb--black-silhouettes.scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W285 has clear radiating wavy lines around its dark mass — the draft's chapter 1 description of it as having almost no radiating marks is incorrect; it belongs with the radiating-field works, not the 'silhouette alone' opener. Corrected by moving W285 to chapter 2 and replacing it in chapter 1 with W047, which genuinely has minimal surrounding marks relative to the others.

W047 observation notes jagged lines fanning left and upward, but the larger image confirms the figure is a bird/duck-like silhouette on a diagonal black slope against green — the draft's 'round-bodied figure' description is acceptable at this resolution but 'curved neck' is more accurate than 'round-bodied'; prose corrected to avoid overclaiming.

W010 draft description says 'zigzag lines scatter in every direction' but the anchor image shows lines radiating outward from the head/shoulders area, not from the lower body or grass strip — corrected to 'from the head and shoulders outward'.

W158 anchor image confirms the figure is a cat in a reclining/alert pose on a black shelf, with yellow-green spiral eyes and white fang marks, and radiating yellow lines across the orange field — observations are accurate; the draft's 'crouched' is acceptable.

W285 anchor image confirms the dark form is an elephant-like shape with a trunk and lavender inner contour lines, and the radiating lines are clearly present around the whole form — the draft's chapter 1 placement as a near-markless silhouette is wrong and corrected.

W093 observations note 'a large yellow square and a broad white frame' — the image confirms this is a white-framed work with a yellow interior field and a small black figure at lower right; the draft prose is accurate.

W177 is visibly the most complex work — layered paint-like marks, a large spiral eye, yellow bar forms at the bottom — the draft's description is accurate and its placement as penultimate in chapter 4 is appropriate.
W248 background is confirmed as flat color blocks with loose crossing lines; the draft's description is accurate.
W146 is a teal figure on dark grey with a jagged crown and red marks on the face — confirmed accurate.
W208 shows a side-facing head in near-total black with a thin pink-mauve contour, a small eye cluster, and red mouth mark — confirmed accurate.
W243 shows a large black rounded head on deep red with yellow outlines, concentric circle eyes, white dashed stitching, and isolated blue marks — confirmed accurate.

Transition from W037 to W285 in original chapter 1 referenced 'spiral eye replaced by white X' — this is valid but W285 also has prominent radiating lines making it a poor fit for 'silhouette alone'; corrected by restructuring.
Chapter 1 now uses W093, W037, W047 — all three have minimal or no radiating field marks relative to the rest of the set, making the chapter coherent.

Chapter 2 now includes W285, W010, W062, W179 — all have prominent radiating fields; W285's radiating lines are dark on lavender rather than yellow on warm ground, providing useful contrast within the chapter.
W047 moved to chapter 1: its jagged lines fan in one direction only and are sparse compared to the full-surround radiating fields of W010, W062, W179, W285 — an honest fit for the reduced chapter.

nnotb--black-silhouettes.title: Scrimshaw: Shape, Mark, Field
nnotb--black-silhouettes.question: How many marks does a sealed dark shape require before it reads as a presence?
nnotb--black-silhouettes.introduction: Fifteen works share a common structure: a dark silhouette, a flat field of color, and a small number of marks. This exhibition follows that structure from its most stripped-down form to its most layered, asking at each stop what the marks add and what the unbroken areas of the shape withhold.
nnotb--black-silhouettes.closing: Each work returns to the same arrangement: a sealed form, a few marks, a flat field. What that combination produces — and whether it is sufficient — the shapes leave open.

chapters.title: The Shape Alone
chapters.introduction: Three works open with the most reduced version of the structure: one dark shape, one flat field, and almost nothing else added to either.

stops.whyHere: The smallest, most isolated figure in the exhibition: a rounded black form in a wide yellow field, its stitched grin and looped eyes the only marks that break the seal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #62

stops.whyHere: A low black dome on teal; a single spiral eye is the sole interior mark, the wide empty field above left unbroken.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W093 sits in open yellow warmth at lower right; this shape presses to the ground on cool teal, same economy of marks, different weight and temperature.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #103

stops.whyHere: A bird-like silhouette on saturated green; jagged lines fan in one direction only, and two yellow X-eyes with a stitched mouth are the sole color on the form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W037's single spiral eye gives way to paired X-eyes here; the radiating lines shift from a full arc to a one-sided fan, keeping the field mostly open.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #112

chapters.title: Fields Filled with Lines
chapters.introduction: Four works surround the silhouette with radiating lines that extend across the field in every direction, describing the space around the figure rather than the figure itself.

stops.whyHere: A dark rounded mass on lavender, wavy lines radiating outward from its entire edge; inner lavender contour lines and a detached oval below are the only marks on the form itself.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W047's lines fan to one side on green; here dark lines radiate from all sides on a cool lavender field, and the form turns inward rather than outward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #268

stops.whyHere: A wide-armed silhouette on amber; zigzag lines scatter outward from the head and shoulders across the whole field, denser on the left, while a grass strip anchors the base.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W285's dark lines on lavender give way to black zigzags on warm amber — the radiating marks grow more agitated and the palette heats up.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #88

stops.whyHere: A one-legged figure on orange; two distinct line rhythms — tight zigzags above, slower waves below — give the surrounding space a split quality that the figure's unresolved stance echoes.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W010's lines radiate uniformly from a static form; here the lines divide into two registers around a figure whose balance is itself unresolved.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #92

stops.whyHere: A squat, stepped black shape on olive-yellow; yellow lines pulse outward in all directions while a zigzag mouth reads as snarl or grin depending on the moment.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W062's single-legged instability gives way to a wide, grounded frontality — but the all-direction radiating lines and ambiguous mouth sustain the pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #60

chapters.title: The Eye Mark
chapters.introduction: Four works place the eye at the center of attention, each using a different form — loop, spiral, concentric ring — producing a different quality of looking back at the viewer.

stops.whyHere: Double-loop yellow eyes and a W-shaped mouth on a teal-grounded rabbit form; the eyes hold the gaze with an alertness that the radiating lines behind the figure amplify.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W179's zigzag mouth drew attention across the lower face; here the double-loop eyes pull focus upward and hold it, making the face the primary event.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #98

stops.whyHere: A pointed black form on teal with a single yellow spiral eye; tight zigzags near the jagged mouth and loose waves at the margins give the watchfulness a directional edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W145's frontal double eyes become a single side-facing spiral here — the gaze narrows and points rather than stares outward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #64

stops.whyHere: A reclining black cat on burnt-orange, its yellow-green spiral eyes wide and its white fang-points the only break in the silhouette; yellow lines vibrate across the whole field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W238's cool teal field gives way to hot orange; the spiral eye form recurs but doubles, and white fang marks add a second point of interior detail.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #51

stops.whyHere: A large black rounded head on deep red, its concentric circle eyes and dashed seam-line giving it a wired, assembled quality; isolated blue marks float at the margins apart from the central form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W158's orange field and radiating lines shift to deep red; the eye form moves from spiral to concentric ring, and the surrounding field gains isolated floating marks rather than a continuous radiated field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #147

chapters.title: When the Shape Opens
chapters.introduction: The final four works complicate the silhouette structure: color enters the form, surfaces accumulate marks, and the boundary between figure and field begins to break down.

stops.whyHere: A teal figure on dark grey — color fills the form rather than surrounding it; a jagged crown and two small red marks concentrate pressure on the face from inside the outline.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W243's black form on red is replaced by a colored form on dark grey — the silhouette logic inverts, and the marks move inside the outline rather than into the field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #266

stops.whyHere: A black side-profile held by a thin pink contour; a small blue-white eye cluster and a red mouth mark read as sparks against the dark mass, while zigzag lines continue down the torso.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W146's teal fill gives way to near-total black; the red marks shrink to a single mouth point, and the agitation spreads from face down through the body.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #277

stops.whyHere: A head in three-quarter view where the left side dissolves into layered color marks and a dense tangle of lines; the right eye socket holds a large white spiral that pulls the gaze inward against the surrounding density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W208's restless lines are held within a clear outline; here the outline breaks on one side and the interior marks spill outward, collapsing the boundary between figure and field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #70

stops.whyHere: The most layered work in the exhibition: a black mass with framed eye zones, tooth rows, and a background of flat color blocks crossed by loose lines — the silhouette strategy at its most loaded.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W177's partial dissolution becomes total here; the background is no longer a single flat field but a patchwork of color blocks, and the figure's features multiply into confrontational density.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #165

nnotb--gesture-and-stance.title: Bodies in Motion, Drawings at Rest
nnotb--gesture-and-stance.question: Which lines in a still drawing make a body read as moving rather than stopped?
nnotb--gesture-and-stance.introduction: Twenty-seven drawings, each built around a body caught mid-action: leaning, lunging, bowing, spreading wide, or folding inward. None of these figures are at rest, yet none are photographs of motion. The gallery asks you to track how line, weight, and surrounding space can make a fixed mark read as a body still in the middle of something.
nnotb--gesture-and-stance.closing: Each drawing fixes a body at one instant. Whether that instant reads as arrival, departure, or suspension depends on which line you follow first — and the drawings offer no single answer.

chapters.title: Bodies That Expand Outward
chapters.introduction: Five figures whose limbs, marks, or silhouettes push toward the edges of the frame, testing how far a body can extend before its outline loses coherence.

stops.whyHere: Raised arm, kicked leg, and sweeping white arcs all drive outward from a dense crossed-line core, making expansion the image's central visible fact.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #54

stops.whyHere: Arms wide, one leg forward, mouth open — the figure lunges in multiple directions at once, but semi-transparent layered loops let the olive ground show through the body.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both figures throw limbs outward across their grounds, but where W004 is built on dense colored strokes, W122 uses transparent loops that dissolve the body's edges.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #32

stops.whyHere: Splayed limbs radiate in all directions; dense overlapping loops build the body and the squared, open-toothed face amplifies the sense of outward force to its loudest point in the chapter.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W122's transparency gives way to dense tangled loops, and the open mouth shifts from a lunge into something closer to a shout.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #47

stops.whyHere: One arm arcs wide, the other drops low, pulling the figure into an asymmetric stretch readable as mid-fall or mid-reach rather than display.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The all-directions explosion of W249 narrows here to a single diagonal pull between two unequal arms, making the imbalance more precise and quieter.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #18

stops.whyHere: A single large arching white outline curves over a dense cluster of upright colored lines — no figure, but the same outward-then-inward pull of the chapter's poses rendered as pure line and mark.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W161's asymmetric figure gives way to a composition without a readable body: the arching curve and crowded verticals carry the chapter's tension between expansion and compression in abstract form.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #44

chapters.title: Figures That Hold Their Ground
chapters.introduction: Six figures that stand squarely or crouch forward, occupying their space with a directness that sits between ceremony and confrontation, facing the viewer without retreating.

stops.whyHere: Arms out, feet planted in three flat rectangular shapes, the figure braces against the frame — rigid, wired, and facing the viewer without flinching.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After W245's abstract curve, a figure snaps into view with bilateral symmetry: both arms level, both feet grounded, the body locked into a confrontational square.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #29

stops.whyHere: Wide hat, spread arms, ribcage visible through bright torso stripes — the figure plants itself on a flat teal ground, grin exposed, with no depth to retreat into.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W013's rigid outline gives way to warm color and a grinning face, but the spread-arm, feet-planted stance is identical, shifting tone without changing posture.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #30

stops.whyHere: Oversized scribbled head, one arm raised with a pointing finger, one arm extended right, legs crossed below — a wide reach above a narrow, unstable base.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W270's grin and bright hat are replaced by a dense multi-color scribbled head on dark teal; the arms stay wide but the crossed legs introduce instability beneath.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #46

stops.whyHere: A flat cyan profile figure stands on deep red, both arms extended forward at different heights, fingers spread — the profile stance and uneven reach hold the ground while keeping the gesture open-ended.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W125's frontal pose and scribbled density give way to a clean flat profile: two colors only, the figure simplified to silhouette, the gesture shifted from display to reach.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #264

stops.whyHere: Crouching, splayed, claws visible at the corners — the figure pushes toward the viewer from a void, its red X eyes and bared teeth making the confrontation explicit.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W070's clean flat profile gives way to dense scribbled mass on black; the profile stance becomes a frontal crouch, and the open gesture becomes a push toward the viewer.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #33

stops.whyHere: Upright with pointed ears and flower-ring eyes, the figure holds its ground while zigzag bands cut across it like interference, making alertness and disruption coexist in the same form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W006's void-black ground opens into a blue-purple wash, and the cancellation marks become flower rings — confrontation softened but not resolved.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #242

chapters.title: Bodies in Transit
chapters.introduction: Six figures caught at angles that read as momentum — pitching forward, tilting sideways, or suspended between a step and a stumble, held at an unstable point.

stops.whyHere: The figure pitches forward on comb-toothed feet, one arm raking right, its skeleton visible through a window of clashing color blocks inside the tilted torso.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From W215's upright alertness, the body tips forward here: the confrontational stance becomes a lean, and the interior becomes literally transparent.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #31

stops.whyHere: Steep forward pitch, one foot planted on a hard diagonal ground line, the other leg trailing — dense crossed lines fill the body while red marks locked inside the head stay contained.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W050's warm amber ground is replaced by a yellow-green field split by a hard black diagonal, sharpening the sense that the figure is about to cross a threshold.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #55

stops.whyHere: A hooked limb and absent arm tip a compact figure into a stance readable as a bow, a stumble, or a ceremony — the asymmetry keeps all three readings open.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W286's full-body lurch compresses here into a single asymmetric detail: one hooked arm versus no arm, a smaller imbalance with a quieter, more ambiguous charge.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #258

stops.whyHere: A dark silhouette leans back hard, oversized head swinging wide to the right, forked lines floating free above the solid mass — the lean is away from the viewer rather than toward it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W114 tips forward; W028 tips backward, reversing the direction of imbalance while keeping the same high-contrast two-color flatness.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #263

stops.whyHere: Steep forward lean, X-marked eyes, long fingers nearly grazing the ground — the figure stays upright while reading as mid-collapse, held by a single vertical axis.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W028's backward lean reverses into a forward drop; where W028 is a flat silhouette, W054 is a detailed figure whose crossed-out eyes and dangling hands make the tilt feel exhausted.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #121

stops.whyHere: Two forms share weight without touching: an isolated limb on the left and a compressed spiked mass above, connected only by trailing lines that pull the eye downward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W054's single figure nearly touching the ground gives way to a split composition — the body divided into separate parts, the lean distributed across a gap rather than held in one form.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #148

chapters.title: Figures That Turn Inward
chapters.introduction: Six figures whose postures close rather than open: bowed heads, arms that block rather than reach, and bodies compressed within their surrounding pictorial space.

stops.whyHere: One pale arm raised to cover the face entirely, yellow-orange pressing in from every edge — the gesture closes the figure off rather than extending it outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After W038's divided, suspended forms, a single arm performs the opposite of reach: it blocks, turning the body inward against a bright, insistent surround.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #137

stops.whyHere: Head bowed, wrists crossed low, gold-olive mass spreading across the shoulders — the figure withdraws while black lines scratch outward around it in all directions.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W051's blocking arm is replaced by crossed wrists and a bowed head; the gesture of closure becomes more deliberate, and the surrounding marks grow more agitated.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #138

stops.whyHere: A hooded figure holds its ground at center, face compressed and eyes low, while diagonal rain-like lines press down from all sides and a bright band sits remote at the top edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W227's warm red-amber glow behind withdrawal becomes a cold dark field here, and the surrounding pressure shifts from scratched lines to falling diagonals.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #191

stops.whyHere: The figure bends forward, head down, lines fanning outward from the skull — the bow reads as strain, and the yellow X at the neck is the only color accent in a flat pink field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W246's hooded stillness gives way to a bent posture with lines radiating from the head, making the inward turn visible as physical pressure rather than concealment.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #126

stops.whyHere: Eyes closed, face sealed, the figure stands still while horizontal fabric bands compress the torso and a wide gold skirt fans outward — stillness held inside a layered structure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W230's radiating strain settles here into complete stillness: no lean, no bow, just a closed face and a body wrapped in tight horizontal bands that contain rather than release.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #50

stops.whyHere: A sweeping dark skirt-form dominates the lower half while frayed orange-red lines erupt on the right — the figure is split between a contained sweep and an unraveling edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W099's compressed stillness opens at the edges here: the skirt sweeps wide and the right side frays into loose lines, making containment and dispersal visible in the same image.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #48

chapters.title: The Body Showing Its Frame
chapters.introduction: Four figures in which the skeleton, outline, or interior construction becomes the subject — bodies that are simultaneously solid and see-through at the same time.

stops.whyHere: Arms spread, ribcage lines in pink and red visible through the torso, a radiating tutu shape at the waist — the figure displays its own construction as part of the pose.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W068's fraying edge gives way to a figure that makes its internal structure the central visible fact: ribs, joints, and skirt-spokes all equally exposed on a quiet olive ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #17

stops.whyHere: An inverted skeletal form descends through horizontal bands, bones loosely drawn with gaps between outline and fill — the structure is visible but incomplete, suspended rather than solid.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W289's upright skeletal figure tips upside-down here, and the quiet olive ground becomes a saturated red field crossed by dark horizontal bands that read as both shadow and barrier.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #25

stops.whyHere: A black angular figure leans forward, its interior visible only through two coiled spirals burning inside the wedge-shaped head — structure concentrated into a single charged zone.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W284's distributed skeletal gaps give way to a solid black silhouette where the only interior detail is locked inside the head, making the contrast between opacity and exposure more stark.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #49

stops.whyHere: A large face fills the frame, tan planes marking its structure while yellow zigzags cross it like interference — the face as architecture, hands held at the lower edges without reaching.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W214's full-body silhouette zooms into a single face here, and the structural lines shift from interior spirals to surface interference, ending the gallery at the body's most legible surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #295

nnotb--figures-in-company.title: Figures in Company
nnotb--figures-in-company.question: What visible feature — gap, overlap, shared mark, or mirrored posture — tips separate figures into a group?
nnotb--figures-in-company.introduction: Twenty-three works line this gallery, each placing two or more figures in the same space. The question is not whether they belong together but how the visible evidence — gap, overlap, shared mark, mirrored posture — tips a collection of bodies toward something that reads as a group. Follow the progression and decide for yourself where that threshold falls.
nnotb--figures-in-company.closing: Proximity, shared marks, and overlapping outlines each make a different claim about what joins figures together. The threshold between separate and together remains a question the works leave open.

chapters.title: Two in a Field
chapters.introduction: Six works open with pairs separated by open ground. The interval between figures carries as much visual weight as the figures themselves.

stops.whyHere: Two black figures on flat blue share yellow facial marks — X-eyes on the larger, spiral eyes on the smaller — across open, uncluttered space: similarity without contact.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #106

stops.whyHere: Two figures on purple also hold apart, but visual weight differs sharply: one open and white, one dense and black, the gap charged by contrast rather than likeness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works place exactly two figures on a flat, uncluttered ground with deliberate empty space between them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #257

stops.whyHere: Two flat black figures on red close the gap just enough to form a heart shape between their raised arms — the first moment of deliberate contact in the gallery.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the purple-ground pair never reaches toward each other, these two meet at center, their arms completing a shared form neither could make alone.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #58

stops.whyHere: A large and a small figure share a magenta field without touching; yellow zigzags scatter between them, filling the gap with static rather than connection.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The heart shape of the previous work gave contact a clear sign; here the space between figures is filled with marks that suggest charge without resolving into gesture.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #89

stops.whyHere: Two gaunt jointed figures share an unbroken orange field; one raises a cone toward its own head, the other crouches low — parallel actions that do not address each other.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a flat single-color ground with no depth cues, so the figures' relationship depends entirely on posture and proximity rather than setting.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #28

stops.whyHere: One expansive open-mouthed figure faces a compact scowling bird-like figure across an open middle ground — the most explicit face-to-face orientation so far.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The orange-field pair acted in parallel without facing each other; here the two figures are oriented directly toward one another, and the background carries loose marks rather than remaining flat, adding pressure to the gap between them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #9

chapters.title: Marks Held in Common
chapters.introduction: Five works explore figures that share repeated visual marks — crossed eyes, spiked crowns, coiled lines — as if the marks themselves are what connects them.

stops.whyHere: Two figures carry nearly identical red-circled cross-marked heads against a yellow field; the doubling reads as a bond written directly onto each face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous chapter's pairs were linked by posture and proximity; here the connection is inscribed in matching marks on each figure's head.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #136

stops.whyHere: Two large black figures share crossed X-eyes, ringed circles, and tooth rows; the repeated marks stack and overlap until the figures feel like one dense system.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use identical head-marks to link their figures, but here the figures press closer together, their shared marks beginning to merge rather than simply echo.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #249

stops.whyHere: Two black animal-like figures carry the same red X-eyes and yellow outlines as the previous work, but a buzzing lower zone of interlocking rectangles adds a shared environment to the shared marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's figures were linked by marks alone; this one surrounds both figures with a common visual field, so mark and setting together form the bond.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #249

stops.whyHere: Two crowned figures with matching red eyes and splayed hands lean toward each other; the shared crown marks and the striped floor beneath them suggest a theatrical pairing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous pair faced outward with crossed-out eyes, these two face each other, their matching crowns framing the space between them as a kind of stage.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #261

stops.whyHere: Two spiked figures hold each other inside near-black space, their matching disc-eyes and red-loop outlines making the embrace feel like a meeting of similar forms.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The crowned pair leaned toward each other without touching; here the figures make full contact, the shared marks now wrapped inside an actual embrace.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #272

chapters.title: Three and the Space Between Them
chapters.introduction: Five works introduce a third figure, testing whether the addition produces a group or a more complicated arrangement of pairs.

stops.whyHere: Two faces share one compressed space without a shared sightline — one thrown back, one tipped forward — held inside vertical strokes that neither frame nor release them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous chapter ended with two figures in contact; here two faces occupy the same zone yet look in opposite directions, reopening the question of whether proximity equals connection.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #139

stops.whyHere: Three face-like forms share one olive field, the largest anchored by thick gray lines while two smaller versions drift rightward and grow fainter — multiplicity without clear separation.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two-face compression of the previous work becomes three here, the additional forms drifting rather than pressing, suggesting repetition more than grouping.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #297

stops.whyHere: Two skeletal figures at left and a dense coiling mass at right compete for attention; a small pink figure in the corner sits apart, belonging to neither zone.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the olive-field faces shared a single surface, this work splits into competing zones, the small corner figure raising the question of whether a figure outside the main grouping still belongs to it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #233

stops.whyHere: Two broad dark forms stand side by side while a smaller, quieter third form sits apart to the right — the clearest spatial diagram of majority and outlier in the exhibition.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works place a smaller figure at the edge of a larger grouping, but here the teal ground holds all three at a cool, legible distance that makes the separation explicit.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #197

stops.whyHere: A large warm central figure is surrounded by multiple small circular eye-forms drifting across the left; a wandering white line threads near them without connecting them to the center.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's three figures were spatially distinct; here the smaller forms multiply and scatter, so the question of grouping becomes one of diffusion rather than arrangement.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #3

chapters.title: Bodies Pressed Together
chapters.introduction: Three works move from proximity to overlap, where figures share outlines or surfaces and individual boundaries become difficult to trace.

stops.whyHere: Two head shapes occupy the same space without fully merging — one flat orange, one softer and receding — their overlapping edges making separation feel unstable.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous chapter's figures were scattered across open ground; here two heads press into the same zone, their edges blurring the boundary between one figure and another.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #289

stops.whyHere: Three upright forms dissolve into overlapping rectangles in orange, teal, and yellow-green; the white outlines read as bodies, but the stacked geometry makes them hard to count.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two-head overlap of the previous work becomes three figures here, their edges further dissolved by geometric layering until individual bodies are difficult to isolate.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #22

stops.whyHere: Two heavy black forms face each other across a field packed with neon grids and hatched rectangles; the crossed circles inside each read as eyes, giving the dense compression a confrontational axis.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's figures were tangled in overlapping colored strokes; here the compression is architectural — neon grids and hatched bands fill every gap, leaving the two forms no room to separate.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #6

chapters.title: The Group as a Single Thing
chapters.introduction: Seven works close the exhibition with figures so close, so numerous, or so uniformly marked that the group itself becomes the subject rather than any individual within it.

stops.whyHere: Three figures press together against black, their crossing orange and teal lines merging at the edges; the shared features and tight grouping make the trio read as one dense entity.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous chapter's pairs were compressed by geometry and ground; here three figures share a physical mass, their overlapping lines making the group feel like a single organism.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #13

stops.whyHere: Seven figures stand shoulder to shoulder across the full width, their scribbled heads blazing orange-yellow; the row reads as a collective charge rather than a set of individuals.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three figures formed a tight cluster in the previous work; here seven press across the entire width, the group now filling the frame completely.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #12

stops.whyHere: Four spiked figures of different sizes crowd the space, linked by blue scribble lines that weave through all of them — shared atmosphere rather than shared outline.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The seven-figure row was unified by identical posture and a shared color band; here four figures differ in size and position but are woven together by a common field of blue marks.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #117

stops.whyHere: Roughly eighteen small figures scatter across white space, each sharing the same rough vocabulary of round body and pointed ears but tilted in a different direction — the group held together by type rather than proximity or contact.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's four figures were linked by a shared atmospheric field; here the group is held together only by shared form, with open white space between every member.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #132

The closing chapter description of W029 as having 'no face' is supportable but the whyHere text invents a 'split face from abstraction vertically' in the transition that refers to W233 — W233 does not split face from abstraction vertically, it has overlapping heads throughout; transition corrected.

W176 anchor image confirms: the amber-yellow field is correct; four distinct face-like forms are visible including the upper-left black figure with yellow eyes, the central figure with teal spiral eyes, the right-center figure with blue rectangular eyes, and the lower-right animal-like head. The 'warm amber-yellow field' description is accurate. The reading's claim of 'four open-mouthed forms' is supported.

W297 anchor image confirms: flat yellow rectangle upper two-thirds, black silhouetted rounded forms along lower edge with XX marks, zigzag lines in yellow above the silhouettes. The 'eight or nine' count is approximately correct at this resolution. The 'crossed marks' are XX not simple crosses — description is accurate enough.

W210 and W233 are visually very similar (both show overlapping toothy heads with cyan passages). The draft places them consecutively in Chapter 4, which is defensible as a contrast pair, but the transition claiming W233 is 'denser' and 'legibility harder won' is a fine-detail claim that cannot be fully verified at thumbnail resolution; softened to a visible structural observation.

The 'white bar cluster' is visible. The chapter 4 placement of W045 as an 'ambiguous mass' is honest given the image.

W134 transition from W045 claims 'depth is suggested by a black sky and spatial separation' — the black sky with X marks and three spatially separated figures is confirmed in the image. Transition is supportable.

W124 transition from W204 claims the face is 'buried in color masses' in W204 — the red-outlined face in W204 is actually visible near the bottom center, not buried; revised to note it is surrounded rather than buried.

W086 observation mentions 'A large arched form in olive and brown' — the image shows a large form that reads as olive/brown/gold, broadly accurate. The 'smaller open-mouthed figure with visible teeth sits at upper left' is confirmed.

nnotb--crowded-crossings.title: Finding Faces in a Crowd
nnotb--crowded-crossings.question: Which visible features — outline, color, scale, or gap — let one face hold its place in a crowded drawing?
nnotb--crowded-crossings.introduction: These twenty drawings share a single problem: too many marks, too many forms, too many possible faces. Some works announce their figures immediately; others place them beneath crossing lines and competing shapes. Moving through the gallery, notice what draws your eye to one face over another — outline, color, scale, or simply the gap between two marks.
nnotb--crowded-crossings.closing: Whether a face holds its place depends on what the drawing withholds as much as what it shows. Each work draws that line differently.

chapters.title: One Face, Clearly There
chapters.introduction: These works open with figures that remain readable — faces that give the eye a place to land before the surrounding marks begin to accumulate.

stops.whyHere: Black silhouettes press upward against a flat yellow field; their shared XX marks make each head legible while the group reads as a single mass.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #119

stops.whyHere: A single hatted figure fills the frame; the contained head above and dissolving strokes below show one face holding while the rest of the image comes apart.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From anonymous silhouettes to a distinct individual: the hat and concentric eye rings give this figure a specificity the crowd below lacked.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #276

stops.whyHere: A large face crowds the picture edge, its layered eyes watchful; the fragmented lower blocks split the image into face and surrounding noise.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The hatted figure was centered and stable; here the face presses to the frame edge, making legibility feel more pressured and less settled.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #251

stops.whyHere: A skull holds center against a teal ground while color lines pull outward; hollow eye sockets keep the face readable through absence rather than mark.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face was built from rings and fills; this one is structured by voids — the empty eye sockets make the skull legible through what is missing.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #208

chapters.title: Faces Multiplying
chapters.introduction: Recognizable figures begin to repeat — mouths, eyes, and heads recur across the surface until no single face commands the space alone.

stops.whyHere: A skull contains a second face within it, while a smaller sun-face occupies the corner; three distinct presences share one image without merging.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The skull in the previous work was singular and centered; here a second face nests inside the first, introducing the idea of faces containing faces.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #0000

stops.whyHere: Three toothed mouths stack inside one bulging purple-red form, each paired with coiled eye marks — faces nested within a face, the surface layered and pressured.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The nesting in the previous work was spatial — one skull around another; here three mouths are built into a single form's body.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #10

stops.whyHere: A large circle on cobalt blue holds a heart, a flower, and a striped wedge that reads as a grin; competing interior forms make the circle itself feel face-like.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work nested faces explicitly; here the face is implied — a circle whose interior accumulates enough features to read as a head without declaring itself one.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #176

stops.whyHere: Dozens of small oval faces ring the border while larger open-mouthed figures crowd the center; the image is entirely populated, with no neutral ground remaining.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work held its forms inside one circle; here faces escape every boundary, lining the edges and filling the center simultaneously.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #71

stops.whyHere: A broad arched form anchors the center while a smaller snarling figure crowds the upper left; two figures at different scales pull against each other without resolving.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work distributed faces evenly across the surface; here scale difference creates tension — one large form, one small intruder, neither yielding.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #221

chapters.title: The Crowd Turns Loud
chapters.introduction: Color and mark-making intensify. Mouths open, lines multiply, and the drawings become harder to read as any single coherent scene.

stops.whyHere: Four open-mouthed forms crowd an amber field, each built from looping spirals and jagged teeth; white lines move freely across all of them, refusing to settle into any one figure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work held two figures in tension; here four faces press forward simultaneously, the amber ground pushing them all toward the viewer at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #183

stops.whyHere: Five spiky-ringed faces crowd a near-black ground; a lone pink flower and yellow spiral above the central figure are the only calm shapes in an otherwise agitated surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The warm amber ground of the previous work is replaced by near-black; the faces are now ringed by jagged lines rather than looping ones, sharpening the sense of agitation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #182

stops.whyHere: Six oval heads rise in a row, mouths open, bodies dissolving into white vertical streaks; soft pink background circles pull against the density of the figures above.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work scattered its faces across the field; here they line up in a row, introducing order — but the dissolving bodies undercut any sense of stability.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #14

stops.whyHere: Five round-headed figures are pressed forward by white outlines against loud color bands; two open mouths range from wide grin to dark gap, keeping the gathering's mood unresolved.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous row of heads dissolved downward into streaks; these figures are outlined and edge-sharp, holding their form even as the color bands behind them compete.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #43

stops.whyHere: Black rectangular masses and hot color zones pack the plane; a red-outlined face near the bottom — wide eyes, open mouth, arms spread — reads as surrounded by the surrounding density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work used white outlines to separate figures from ground; here no such separation exists — the face sits inside the same density as everything around it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #177

chapters.title: Figures Crossing, Lines Taking Over
chapters.introduction: These works push toward maximum density. Figures overlap until one form's edge becomes another's body, and the final work tests whether a face was ever fully there.

stops.whyHere: A seated central figure extends limbs outward while bared teeth recur at the margins; a floating white rectangle holds open a gap in the surrounding density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work surrounded its face with color masses; here a figure has limbs and posture, but repeated mouth fragments at the edges keep it from reading as singular.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #19

stops.whyHere: Three figures caught mid-action — arms raised, teeth out, dome swelling between them — share a black sky without any one commanding the space; spectacle and unease coexist.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's figures were pressed flat by color; here a black sky and spatial separation suggest depth, yet the figures still compete rather than recede.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #254

stops.whyHere: A dark mass holds center against an orange field while blue slashes cut across at angles; the white bar cluster reads as both noise and anchor in a composition that refuses to settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work distributed figures across a legible space; here the central form is ambiguous — mass rather than figure — and crossing diagonals deny any stable reading.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #238

stops.whyHere: Several toothy heads overlap with raised limb-like forms; broad cyan passages open brief gaps, but one face's outline keeps becoming part of another's body.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's ambiguity came from a single dominant mass; here multiple heads compete, and the cyan gaps are the only breathing room in the tangle.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #1

stops.whyHere: Heads and limb-like forms weave together in colored marks; the drawing alternates between recognizable characters and almost illegible crossings, making looking a repeated act of finding and losing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works share overlapping heads and cyan passages, but here the colored marks layer more completely over the figures, making each face harder to hold.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #1 fork

stops.whyHere: Yellow strokes, a red spiral cluster, and crossing lines fill the field without resolving into a face; any figure found here is the viewer's own construction.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work still offered recognizable heads amid the crossings; here the marks no longer assemble into a face — the question the gallery opened with goes unanswered.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #193
