nnotb--creatures-and-objects.title: What Makes a Shape a Character?
nnotb--creatures-and-objects.question: Which specific marks — an eye shape, a posture, a mouth line — are enough to make a shape read as a character?
nnotb--creatures-and-objects.introduction: Twenty-six works line this gallery, ranging from figures whose species reads at a glance to forms where a face is barely implied. Each stop asks you to notice the specific marks — an eye shape, a posture, a mouth line — that trigger recognition. The journey moves from clear silhouettes toward ambiguity and back, testing where character begins and ends.
nnotb--creatures-and-objects.closing: A spiral, a bared tooth, a crossed eye, a shadow — any one of these can be enough to tip a shape into a character. The threshold keeps shifting from work to work.

chapters.title: Silhouette and Signal
chapters.introduction: Four figures whose outlines read immediately as animal or creature, each using a different minimum set of marks to confirm that reading.

stops.whyHere: A flat yellow beak and single visible eye are the minimum signals needed; dense layered strokes do the rest of the character work.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #56

stops.whyHere: Where W009 uses layered colour to build volume, here a flat black silhouette on acid-green does the same job with almost nothing — two orange spirals and a jagged mouth suffice.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From dense painterly marks to pure flat silhouette: both figures read instantly, but by opposite means.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #122

stops.whyHere: Pink on black, a long toothed snout and spiked crest — the silhouette is unambiguous, yet the thick wavy neck-line fractures the form just enough to introduce doubt.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The flat-on-flat logic continues, but the fractured neck introduces a crack in the clean silhouette that W119 never allowed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #265

stops.whyHere: Two black masses share a blue field; the smaller one's yellow rectangular eyes and stitched mouth confirm character while the larger form stays mute beside it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W293 is a single loud pink shape; here two black forms share the frame, and only one carries the face marks — the other remains ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #133

chapters.title: Bodies and Posture
chapters.introduction: Figures whose stance — arched, hunched, braced, or crouching — carries as much descriptive weight as any mark on the face.

stops.whyHere: An extreme arched pose balanced on a single sphere; the body's position reads as alarm or display before the spiral eyes confirm it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from a static silhouette pair to a figure caught mid-action: posture now does the character work the face was doing before.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #53

stops.whyHere: Head dropped, spine arched, legs planted — the burdened stance reads before the warm looping lines across the torso add their own layer of unease.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both figures arch their spines, but W137 reads as agitation while W141 reads as weight — the same posture carrying opposite charges.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #284

stops.whyHere: Front-facing, wings spread wide, heavy feet planted — a posture of display or threat, with the small masked face arriving late as a stranger detail.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W141 faces sideways with a lowered head; W065 faces directly out, wings thrown open — the shift from private strain to public confrontation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #39

stops.whyHere: A crouching figure with feathered shoulder forms and a long toothed mouth; the crouch pulls the body inward while the spread lines push outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W065 stands upright and wide; W172 folds low and forward, the same outward energy now compressed into a crouch.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #27

stops.whyHere: A small upright figure and an enormous coiled mass share the same outline language; scale difference alone creates the tension between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W172 is a single figure whose energy spreads outward; W049 splits that energy between two forms of radically different size.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #40

chapters.title: The Face as Mask
chapters.introduction: Works where the face is drawn as a set of applied marks — spirals, grids, crosses — laid onto a form rather than built into it.

stops.whyHere: Square-spiral eyes and rectangular teeth sit on a black cat mass like a mask laid over a silhouette — the face reads as added, not grown.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W049 uses scale to create unease; W036 uses the gap between a naturalistic silhouette and its mask-like face markings.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #255

stops.whyHere: A black cat form again, but now a white grid covers the body and a flower shape replaces one eye — the figure reads as catalogued or annotated rather than alive.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both are black cat silhouettes with applied face marks, but W036's marks feel decorative while W231's grid reads as inventory.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #246

stops.whyHere: Red crossed lines over both eyes, a pink-blue collar, a thin circle around the head — adornment and obstruction occupy the same marks simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W231's grid covers the whole body; W295 concentrates its applied marks on the face alone, making the crossing-out more pointed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #248

stops.whyHere: Yellow spiral eyes and a jagged mouth on a large teal form flanked by crown-marked shapes — the face is assembled from signals, the surrounding marks repeating them like an echo.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W295 is a single figure with a busy face; W164 spreads the face-signal logic outward into the whole composition.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #155

stops.whyHere: X-marked eyes and an open mouth on a green face, with a small starred burst below repeating the X motif — the face mark becomes a pattern across the image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W164's spiral eyes echo in flanking shapes; W194 takes one eye mark and repeats it at a different scale within the same frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #2

chapters.title: Softness and Its Limits
chapters.introduction: Figures that approach rounded, toy-like familiarity while other visible marks — scribbled surfaces, sealed grins, goggle lenses — pull against that reading.

stops.whyHere: Balloon-like limbs and a flat yellow surround suggest a toy, but spiral eye rings and surface scribbles sit visibly on top, refusing to let the softness settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W194's marks read as alarm; W197 uses similar layered marks on a form that invites comfort — the same technique, a different starting point.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #111

stops.whyHere: A hunched figure assembled from restless layered lines that never close into solid mass; the orange goggle eyes glow inward rather than outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W197 is rounded and toy-like; W116 is similarly soft in outline but the body never solidifies — the comfort is less available here.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #99

stops.whyHere: Bands of white and grey wrap a bulbous figure completely; two black disc lenses and a packed-tooth grin read as cheerful and sealed at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W116's body is open and semi-transparent; W271's is wrapped tight — both withhold something, but by opposite means.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #275

stops.whyHere: A crowned white figure with loose open lines holds the center while smaller figures — bird, cat, distant form — occupy the edges without competing for its weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W271 is a single sealed form; W091 opens the frame to multiple presences, the central figure's looseness contrasting with W271's tight wrapping.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #247

stops.whyHere: Three zones share one field without merging: a face-grid that shifts from expressive to blank, a slow spiral creature, a dotted ring — character distributed rather than centred.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W091 has a clear central figure with peripheral presences; W216 refuses a centre, spreading character signals across three separate zones.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #42

chapters.title: Density and the Edge of Recognition
chapters.introduction: Works where layered marks, competing color fields, or compressed scale push the figure toward the limit of readability, held together by the minimum necessary marks.

stops.whyHere: Two glowing spiral eyes and a hidden secondary toothed face compete for attention; the dense hatched body makes both hard to hold at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W216 distributes character across zones; W081 compresses two competing faces into a single dense form.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #79

stops.whyHere: Dense black scribble lines hold a compact form together while flame bursts at head and tail and large reflective eyes pull against the surrounding weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W081's two faces create internal competition; W211 has one face but the body's density and the flame bursts create a similar pull between mass and signal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #59

stops.whyHere: The figure splits sharply between amber glow and near-black; teeth bared, eye half-lidded — the light division does as much character work as the face marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W211's density is uniform across the frame; W241 splits the figure in two by light alone, making half the body a shadow that the face must work against.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #128

stops.whyHere: A heavy creature moves left, teeth bared, its body a tangle of cool lines against a hot orange field — the ambiguity between snarl and grin sits at the centre.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W241's split is warm light against deep black; W019's split is cool body against hot ground — figure and field in active competition.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #66

stops.whyHere: A dark animal head pushes close to the picture edge, gold-ringed eyes built from stacked zigzag lines; figure and warm ground compete for the same plane.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W019's creature moves through its field; W140's head is static but pressed so close to the edge that containment itself becomes uncertain.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #243

stops.whyHere: A stretched near-monochrome figure reaches across most of the frame toward a tiny vivid creature; the wide grey space makes the reach feel effortful and the character feel earned.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W140 is dense and close; W131 is spare and stretched — compression and extension as opposite ways of holding a figure in the frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #129

stops.whyHere: Two blocky upright forms layered with competing vertical colour streaks; paired red oval marks near a rounded mass invite a face reading that never fully resolves.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W131's figure is unmistakable despite its sparseness; W235 offers the minimum marks for a face reading and then withholds confirmation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #35

nnotb--settings-and-light.scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W023 anchor image confirms: the building is surrounded by neon yellow-green and orange verticals with a teal-blue upper zone and a pale blue-grey lower band — observations are accurate. The description 'neon yellow-green marks run vertically' is confirmed but the lower band is more teal-blue than pale blue-grey at full resolution; prose adjusted slightly.

W150 anchor image confirms: the composition shows golden hillsides, a blue river channel left of center, a green ridge form, and a teal-blue sky with black and white looping lines — the draft observation of 'dense overlapping black scribble lines layered over flat color' is accurate for the hillside areas. The sky upper zone is teal with loose black and white lines, not a simple flat color. Prose adjusted to reflect the sky zone.

W290 anchor image confirms: the image has a pale grey-pink upper zone (clouds), a warm amber-orange band, a broad turquoise sweep through the middle, and turbulent maroon/dark lower forms with white looping outlines. The draft description is accurate. The transition from W150 claiming 'same palette pushed toward dissolution' is partially supported — both share amber-gold and blue/teal — but W290 is far more turbulent and abstract while W150 retains legible landscape structure. Transition reworded to be more specific about visible differences.

W072 observations describe 'yellow clusters above dark branching and upright forms' and 'a low row of vertical divisions along the bottom edge.' The anchor image confirms this reads as a tree canopy scene. The transition from W290 to W072 (pressured horizontal zones giving way to vertical movement) is visually supported.

W064 observations describe horizontal white lines over vertical color strokes. The image confirms this. The transition from W072 (canopy yellow reappearing with ruled lines) is supported by both works sharing yellow-orange masses, though W064 is more abstract. Transition is accurate.

W046: the dark figure, white looping forms below, and warm solar disc upper-left are all confirmed in the image. The transition from W064 claiming 'soft yellow masses condense into a single disc' is a reasonable visible correspondence — both works share yellow-orange upper areas. Transition is acceptable.

W098: the large face on yellow-olive field with red-orange eye/mouth accents and white teardrop shapes is confirmed. The transition from W046 claiming 'solar disc has expanded into an entire yellow field' is a reasonable visible link between the warm upper-left disc in W046 and the yellow field in W098. Acceptable.

W133: the rounded head with black hatching, yellow loop arc, and visible teeth are confirmed. The transition from W098 is supported — both show faces under color-field pressure, with the shift from external color field to surface hatching being a genuine visible contrast.

W056: the draft describes this as a 'face-like reading' but the image shows no clear face — it is an abstract composition of light fan, gold/ochre bands, and a heavy black arc. The 'face-like reading' claim is unsupported and has been removed. The work's role is revised to focus on its abstract light-versus-weight dynamic as a contrast to the face works.
W153: the gold-olive mass, diagonal light beam, dark cavity, and background spirals are confirmed. The transition from W056 (light fan narrowing to a beam) is visually supported.
W196: the dome enclosure, gold rays, dark-blue form inside, and floating pale circles are confirmed. The transition from W153 (diagonal beam expanding to radial burst) is supported.

W183: the dark left mass, blazing yellow-gold right field with two white discs, and red blocks at bottom are confirmed. The transition from W196 (contained radiance opening into unenclosed split) is supported.

W041: the two diagonal light beams, nested rectangles, glowing ovals, and dense left scribble edge are confirmed. The transition from W183 (two white discs reappearing as two beams) is a reasonable visible link.

W190: the angular form with two white glowing rectangles, zigzag lines, and dark upper-left cluster are confirmed. The transition from W041 (beams condensing into fixed rectangular sources) is supported.

W219: the horizontal bar with oval recesses, downward triangles, and surrounding zigzag lines are confirmed. The transition from W190 (glowing rectangles becoming oval recesses in a bar) is a reasonable visible correspondence.

nnotb--settings-and-light.title: Ground, Light, Surround
nnotb--settings-and-light.question: When does the space around a subject carry as much visual weight as the subject itself?
nnotb--settings-and-light.introduction: Sixteen works move between open landscape and enclosed figure, between cast light and dense mark. None of them lets the background stay neutral. A building dissolves into its field; a face is split across two color zones; a valley holds as much visual weight as any portrait. Five chapters trace how surrounding space can redirect, contain, or reframe what sits inside it.
nnotb--settings-and-light.closing: Each work leaves the boundary between subject and surround unsettled. Whether that instability comes from light, ground, or enclosing geometry remains an open question across every room.

chapters.title: Grounds That Will Not Recede
chapters.introduction: Three works where the space beneath and around a form is as visually active as anything placed on it — the ground competes rather than supports.

stops.whyHere: A gabled building holds its shape through repeated misaligned outlines while neon yellow-green verticals and a teal lower band compete equally with the structure for attention.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #21

stops.whyHere: Golden hillsides, a blue river channel, and a teal sky built from looping black and white lines make the landscape itself the subject — no single form anchors the field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the building in the previous work was framed by charged marks, here those marks have spread across the entire surface with no structure left to contain them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #158

stops.whyHere: Turquoise sweeps and maroon hollows press against each other across three zones; white looping outlines hold the lower mass together without resolving it into any readable form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works share amber-gold and blue-teal areas, but here the landscape has become far more turbulent and abstract — the legible hillside gives way to churning, interlocked color masses.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #15

chapters.title: Canopy, Cloud, Open Air
chapters.introduction: Three works where marks accumulate into something sky-like or foliage-like, and the boundary between inside and outside becomes genuinely uncertain.

stops.whyHere: Yellow clusters spread above dark upright forms in an arrangement that can suggest trees, with translucent areas softening the boundary between support and canopy.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After the turbulent horizontal zones of the previous work, the vertical movement here — dark forms rising into spreading yellow — introduces a different kind of spatial layering.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #219

stops.whyHere: Horizontal white lines rule across vertical color strokes, holding yellow and orange masses above while blue strokes fall below; the two movements meet without resolving.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The canopy-like yellow of the previous work reappears, but now white ruled lines impose a horizontal order that the color beneath refuses to respect.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #36

stops.whyHere: A dark figure sits amid billowing white loops on a blue-lavender ground while a warm solar disc occupies the upper left — the surrounding air carries as much visual weight as the figure within it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The loose yellow masses of the previous work condense here into a single disc at upper left, and the open field below the figure carries the same diffuse, cloud-like quality the earlier work spread across its whole surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #65

chapters.title: Faces and Fields
chapters.introduction: Four works where a face is surrounded by color zones or enclosing marks that divide or reframe it, plus one abstract field showing what remains when the face is absent.

stops.whyHere: Yellow floods the upper field while olive pools below, splitting the face across two tones; a faint blue rectangle floats over the center like a second, cooler layer pressing in from outside.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The solar disc from the previous work has expanded here into an entire yellow field that the face must occupy rather than observe.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #296

stops.whyHere: Dense black hatching buries the face's surface while a yellow loop arcs outside the form, pulling attention around the figure rather than into it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous face was split by a surrounding color field, this one is buried under hatching — the pressure has moved from the field inward to the surface itself.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #189

stops.whyHere: A broad fan of pale light pushes from the left across gold and ochre bands while a heavy black arc holds the right edge — an abstract field of light against weight, with no face present.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The yellow loop outside the previous figure becomes here a full light source pushing across the frame; the figure has disappeared, leaving only the tension between radiance and dark mass.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #82

stops.whyHere: A gold-olive mass fills the frame, its surface built from crossing scribble lines; a diagonal light beam cuts across the upper left while a dark cavity below reads as tense against the calm background spirals.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The broad light fan of the previous work narrows here into a single diagonal beam, and the mass it strikes is denser and more resistant than the open bands it crossed before.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #84

chapters.title: Light as Enclosure
chapters.introduction: Four works where light does not simply illuminate but surrounds or structures the forms inside it, making the lit space feel sealed rather than open.

stops.whyHere: A form sits sealed inside a dome while gold rays push outward from behind it; the enclosure reads as both lit from within and pressed upon from without, the floating pale circles softening neither reading.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The diagonal beam of the previous work has expanded here into a full radial burst, and the form it surrounds is now literally enclosed rather than merely struck.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #78

stops.whyHere: The image divides between a dark layered left mass and a blazing yellow-gold right field where two white discs burn; red blocks at the bottom sit heavily against that upper light.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The dome's contained radiance opens here into an unenclosed split — light and dark occupy separate halves rather than one surrounding the other.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #180

stops.whyHere: Two hard light beams slice through layered nested rectangles, pulling the eye from a dense scribbled left edge toward glowing ovals that read as sources rather than reflections.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two white discs of the previous work reappear here as two beams cutting through structure rather than burning within an open field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #75

stops.whyHere: Two white-hot rectangles anchor the composition while zigzag lines spread outward in yellow and cyan; a dark compressed cluster at upper left sits in contrast to that brightness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The beams of the previous work have condensed into two fixed rectangular sources, and the surrounding marks now radiate outward from them rather than crossing them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #73

chapters.title: Geometry and Scatter
chapters.introduction: Three works where surrounding space is organized by bars, arches, and zigzag lines that hold or release the forms sitting inside them.

stops.whyHere: A horizontal bar with oval recesses anchors the upper field while downward triangles and surrounding zigzag lines read as noise holding the central forms in charged suspension.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two glowing rectangles of the previous work reappear here as oval recesses in a machine-like bar — the light sources have become inset forms, and the surrounding scatter has become more organised.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #74

stops.whyHere: Two diagonal beams slice through a field of zigzag borders and nested rectangles; glowing spiral cores inside the arched form hold still against all that surrounding movement.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bar and triangles of the previous work give way here to diagonal beams crossing a similarly dense field — the geometry shifts from horizontal to diagonal, and stillness moves from the bar into the spiral cores.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #76 cash lightning

nnotb--letters-and-signs.title: Letters Among the Marks
nnotb--letters-and-signs.question: When a readable word appears inside a painted surface, does it direct looking or compete with it?
nnotb--letters-and-signs.introduction: Across fourteen works, words and symbols appear on the same surface as faces, figures, and dense mark-making. Sometimes a word names what we see; sometimes it sits inside a body or floats as pure shape. Five chapters trace what happens at that boundary — where reading and looking pull in different directions, and neither fully resolves the other.
nnotb--letters-and-signs.closing: Each work places a legible sign inside a field that resists easy reading. Whether the word clarifies or complicates what surrounds it is a question each work answers differently.

chapters.title: The Word Inside the Body
chapters.introduction: Three works carry explicit text absorbed into or standing apart from a figure, treating language as a material element rather than a caption or title.

stops.whyHere: 'BULLISH' floats in semi-transparent red lettering across the bear figure's torso, absorbed into the body rather than sitting cleanly on top of it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #90

stops.whyHere: 'STILL BULLISH @NIFTYINK' appears in solid outlined letters separate from the loose mark-making of the dark horned figure — declaration standing apart from dissolution.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works carry the same word, but here it shifts from transparent overlay into hard-edged block text that stands apart from the figure it accompanies.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #100

stops.whyHere: Two red 'BULLISH' blocks sit at the upper-left and lower-left, holding a dense interior of colliding marks and looping lines between them like brackets around noise.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single word now doubles, anchoring two corners of the left field rather than inhabiting a figure — text functioning as structural device rather than label.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #87

chapters.title: Signs That Behave as Shapes
chapters.introduction: Three works carry marks that resemble writing or symbols but resist full decoding, functioning as visual weight and rhythm rather than readable content.

stops.whyHere: Crown shapes with spirals, blue blocks, and a lime-green oval chain compete as visual events; no single mark resolves into plain meaning.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The explicit word disappears; what remains are symbol-like forms — crowns, spirals, grids — that carry the look of significance without delivering a readable message.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #281

stops.whyHere: White hand-lettered marks run across the mid-section but remain illegible as text, functioning instead as horizontal rhythm against the cross-hatched lower quadrant.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works layer mark types across a busy field, but here a face structure organizes the surface — X-marked oval eyes and an open round mouth hold the center while marks compete around them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #116

stops.whyHere: Loose lettering fills the top band in the same thick outline style as the central forms, making text and image indistinguishable in visual weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The face structure becomes more schematic — two eye-like forms, one a tight spiral and one a cross-hatched rectangle, sit side by side, and the lettering above reads as part of the same drawn system.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #108

chapters.title: Faces Without Anchors
chapters.introduction: Three works build faces from glowing voids, scribbled masses, and competing color zones — present as figures but without the stability a readable sign might provide.

stops.whyHere: Two blown-out light orbs replace eyes entirely, erasing the detail that would anchor expression; the face is present but not fully legible.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After works dense with competing marks, this face strips back to near-darkness — a scribbled mass above and looping jaw below hold a figure together without resolving it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #86

stops.whyHere: Stitched seam lines and bared teeth give the figure visible structure, but the fractured hat and uneven background glow keep it from settling into a stable read.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous face dissolved into light and dark, this one is assembled — seams, teeth, and a layered hat — yet the parts refuse to cohere into a single mood.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #85

stops.whyHere: Coiled white rows, red spikes, and a hard white wedge fill the rounded form's interior, holding the image between a face and something else entirely.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The stitched assembly gives way to a form whose interior splits into competing zones — the coiled lower section reads as teeth or grin, but no dark opening confirms it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #188

stops.whyHere: Heart shapes appear as both central form and repeated smaller motifs; the jagged white outline keeps the familiar symbol unsettled rather than resolved.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The face structure drops away; a recognizable symbol takes its place, but the jagged outline and warm dense field give it the same unresolved quality as the faces before it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #5

chapters.title: Text as Costume and Label
chapters.introduction: Two works place legible text on or near figures as a worn or projected identity, where the word becomes a prop or badge rather than a description.

stops.whyHere: 'SCAFFOLD ETH' hand-lettered on the cauldron pulls the silhouetted figure between emblem and joke, ceremony and deflation held in the same image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The heart symbol gives way to a fully legible label — but the text is on an object the figure bends over, making the word a prop rather than a body marking.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #96

stops.whyHere: 'CCO SUMMER' on a white collar label below the face reads as a tag worn by the yellow figure, while scattered white mark fragments around the black field read as static.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The text moves from object to body — worn as a collar label rather than inscribed on a cauldron — and the figure's blue-framed goggle eyes give it a fixed outward stare the silhouette lacked.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #214

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.introduction: Two works push marks, motifs, text, and assembled parts to every edge simultaneously, testing how much a single surface holds before any hierarchy collapses.

stops.whyHere: Graffiti lettering in the lower-left corner sits beside a mechanical face with lens-bar eyes and a barred mouth unit, treating text as a second layer of address alongside the figure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The collar badge becomes graffiti — text that addresses the viewer from outside the figure rather than being worn by it, while the face itself turns more mechanical and less expressive.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #298

stops.whyHere: Heart-shaped lenses, a concentric-ring target, coil lines, rectangular color blocks, and a row of marks at the mouth all compete across the same layer, making the face feel assembled from colliding parts.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous work splits text and face into distinct zones, here every element crowds the frame at once — motifs, marks, and structural lines refuse any hierarchy.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #107

nnotb--radiating-lines.title: Lines Moving Outward
nnotb--radiating-lines.question: When marks spread away from a central form, what changes as that center becomes more complex or begins to dissolve?
nnotb--radiating-lines.introduction: Seventeen works share one structural habit: lines, waves, zigzags, or spikes move outward from a central form. What those marks carry shifts constantly — from stillness to agitation, from tight order to dispersal. Four chapters follow that spread, tracking what changes when the radiating mark is sparse or dense, and when the center itself starts to break apart.
nnotb--radiating-lines.closing: Each work sends marks outward from something. How those marks read depends on what the center looks like — and how much of it remains visible.

chapters.title: Still Centers, Spreading Lines
chapters.introduction: Three works open with the simplest version: a single dark figure on a flat field, lines fanning outward with almost no competing marks elsewhere on the surface.

stops.whyHere: A seated black rabbit with X eyes sits motionless while yellow zigzag and wave lines spread outward in two registers — tight jolts above, slower rolls to the sides — establishing the exhibition's core tension between still body and active surround.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #91

stops.whyHere: A squat black form on a yellow-green field, red lines radiating outward. The figure is equally inert, but the shift from red ground to acid green sharpens the contrast between body and surround.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works place a motionless black silhouette against a flat saturated field; the color shifts from deep red to sharp yellow-green, changing the temperature of the surrounding scatter.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #61

stops.whyHere: A black mass suspended by a single diagonal line, jagged zigzags spreading across unbroken yellow. The hanging posture introduces precariousness absent from the two seated figures before it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous figures sit grounded on a horizon strip, this form hangs from a taut line, making the radiating marks feel less like heat and more like instability.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #114

chapters.title: The Figure Gains a Face
chapters.introduction: Four works add facial features — eyes, mouths, spiral marks — to the radiating silhouette, asking whether a legible face changes how the surrounding lines read.

stops.whyHere: A rounded black figure with a small disc face sits low in the frame; yellow lines spread outward against deep orange. The face is barely readable, keeping the image close to the previous chapter's silhouettes.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The shift from hanging to seated restores groundedness, and the orange field warms the image, but the figure's minimal face marks a threshold between pure silhouette and readable presence.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #63

stops.whyHere: A black oval with spiral eyes and a serrated grin floats above flat yellow, wavy lines radiating outward, a coiling tether dropping to a small reaching hand in the corner. The face is now fully legible and the mood tips toward unease.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous figure's face was a faint disc; here spiral eyes and a toothed mouth make the center unmistakably expressive, and the radiating lines shift from neutral scatter to something more charged.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #109

stops.whyHere: A reclining animal form packed with yellow cross-hatching, red X eyes, yellow zigzags spreading across blue. The body is no longer upright or floating, and its interior is filled with marks rather than left as flat black.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W104's figure was a clean black oval; here the body is dense with interior scribbling, so the radiating lines outside feel like an extension of internal restlessness rather than external pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #52

stops.whyHere: A stick-limbed figure stands wide-legged, overlapping purple and gold discs spreading behind its upper body, a jagged yellow spiked disc replacing its head. The radiating form has migrated from background lines to the head itself.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous works radiated lines from around the body; here the head is the radiating object — a spiked disc — while the body below remains sketchy and still, reversing the earlier relationship.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #213

chapters.title: Faces That Fill the Frame
chapters.introduction: Four works expand the face until it crowds the available space, and the radiating marks become inseparable from the surface rather than separate from the figure.

stops.whyHere: Three nested circles stack on a red ground, the upper two with red lines branching from blue centers, the lower opening into darkness. The face is now the entire composition, and the radiating marks are inside the eyes.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W128's figure had a body beneath its radiant head; here the body disappears entirely and the radiating marks move inside the eye forms themselves, compressing the spread inward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #24

stops.whyHere: Two paired eyes and a wide toothed mouth fill the frame edge to edge; the background radiates in dense layered stripes of orange, red, yellow, and green. No neutral space remains anywhere in the image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W027's face sat within a bordered red field; here face and radiating background merge so completely that figure and ground become the same dense, pressured surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #118

stops.whyHere: A masked form rises from dense scribbled lines, radiating blue-grey bands spreading behind it. The upper mask is smooth and legible; the lower body dissolves into the radiating marks, blurring the boundary between figure and field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W074's face was flat and frontal; W018 introduces depth and dissolution — the figure emerges from its own radiating marks rather than sitting in front of them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #95

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W018's figure dissolved downward into marks; W188's figure holds its shape but the surrounding field is so dense with competing elements that the radiating lines are just one layer among many.

chapters.title: When the Center Loosens
chapters.introduction: Five works close the exhibition by complicating or dispersing the center through layered spirals, curtained enclosures, and surfaces where radiating mark and ground become indistinguishable.

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W188's radiating lines burst from behind a legible figure; W126 removes the figure entirely, leaving spiral and banded marks to compete without a body to anchor them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #204

stops.whyHere: A large spiral coils from upper-center leftward, its dense core surrounded by horizontal banding, vertical bars, and scattered color patches. Two competing movements — inward spiral and outward bands — keep the surface unsettled.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W126's spiral sat in one corner against flat bands; W170's spiral is larger and its core denser, so the tension between inward pull and outward spread feels more evenly matched.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #239

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #152

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #83

nnotb--bands-and-patterns.title: Divided Surface
nnotb--bands-and-patterns.question: When repeated marks divide a surface, what do they hold together and what do they hold apart?
nnotb--bands-and-patterns.introduction: Twenty-four works share one persistent habit: the repeated mark. Bands slice, zigzags border, grids map, spirals coil, and rows of identical units cross fields of every color. Some surfaces carry recognizable faces; others resist any figure at all. Moving through the gallery, watch how the same devices — stripe, zigzag, grid — can contain a form, fracture it, or replace it entirely.
nnotb--bands-and-patterns.closing: Each work returns to the same question from a different angle: when a surface is divided by repeated marks, the boundary between structure and dissolution stays genuinely open.

chapters.title: Grid Against Face
chapters.introduction: Three works open the gallery by placing a recognizable head inside or against a system of repeated marks, where face and pattern compete for the same space.

stops.whyHere: A yellow oval grid maps the face like a mesh, flattening and exposing it simultaneously; the face is present but held inside a pattern.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #229

stops.whyHere: A three-quarter head on warm brown, its interior packed with zigzag bands and looping zones that replace anatomy with competing mark systems.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the grid in the first work sits over the face as a transparent layer, here the marks have moved inside the head, filling it from within.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #291

stops.whyHere: A frontal rectangular head on cyan, its spiral eyes and grid of yellow blocks pulling against free-running colored lines that ignore the structure entirely.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The three-quarter profile gives way to a blunt frontal rectangle; internal marks shift from organic loops to a hard yellow grid competing with loose scatter.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #164

chapters.title: Frontal Forms, Stacked Zones
chapters.introduction: These works build confrontational frontal structures from horizontal bands and stacked rectangular zones, where pattern takes on the density of architecture.

stops.whyHere: Stacked horizontal zones carry zigzag rows, rounded bumps, and spiral discs; the symmetry reads as confrontational, the marginal lines as restless noise around a blunt signal.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The rectangular head dissolves into pure zone-stacking — no face survives, only the stacked band logic carried to its limit.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #157

stops.whyHere: A flat-fronted form framed by gold border stripes and a magenta-black banded header; scattered yellow circles ring the whole, holding a patterned center in loose enclosure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The purple field and tight symmetry give way to a gold-bordered form whose enclosing circles feel festive rather than confrontational.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #72

stops.whyHere: A circular form whose rectangular band of subdivided cells reads as teeth or keyboard; stacked mechanical panels suggest a face without confirming one.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The scattered circles at the edges become a single dominant circular form here, and the banded zones tighten into something more mechanical and ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #216

stops.whyHere: An assembled stacked form on a wheeled base, every zone packed with saw-tooth and zigzag lines; the thin blue wheels ground the visual noise with an odd stillness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The circular form gains a body and a base — the stacked zone logic extends downward into something that reads as a constructed object.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #273

stops.whyHere: A machine-like central mass on magenta, bordered by coiled shapes; repeated spiral eye motifs create a watchful rhythm against yellow zigzag bands locking the lower section.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The wheeled form is replaced by a denser, borderless mass; zigzag bands migrate to the lower half and the wheeled base becomes a coiled, unwinding edge.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #187

chapters.title: Marks Without a Figure
chapters.introduction: Here the figure recedes or disappears entirely. Bands, grids, and crossing lines take over the full surface, and the question becomes whether any structure holds.

stops.whyHere: An irregular black grid holds warm yellows and burnt reds; white gaps open between strokes, giving the surface a feeling of pressure and release in roughly equal measure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After the magenta figure-field, the figure drops away entirely; what remains is the grid itself, now the sole subject.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #37

stops.whyHere: Rectangular outlines in yellow, magenta, and purple spread across black without locking into a stable grid; a wound central zone and a narrow column suggest containment that keeps slipping.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The warm grid gives way to a cooler black ground; the grid loosens further, its corners open, containment becoming a question rather than a fact.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #41

stops.whyHere: Amber fills every corner; white cross-shapes surface and sink across a field of vertical and horizontal marks that never resolve into a scene.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The black ground flips to saturated amber; rectangular outlines dissolve into individual crossing marks, and structure becomes intermittent.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #11

stops.whyHere: Yellow outline-rectangles stack and overlap like misaligned frames; a red horizontal band cuts across the middle while surrounding loops push toward overflow.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Scattered marks begin to cohere into stacked frames here, but the frames never align — accumulation on the edge of overflow rather than resolution.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #205

stops.whyHere: Yellow presses outward while a black mass anchors center-right; a red-outlined box packed with crossing lines reads as something sealed off from the looser activity around it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Stacked frames give way to a two-force composition — warm field versus dark mass — with one sealed zone of dense crossing lines holding its own against the pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #154

chapters.title: Borders, Rings, and Enclosures
chapters.introduction: Four works use borders, rings, and enclosing lines as their primary device — the mark that travels around a form rather than across it.

stops.whyHere: A wavy border of alternating colored lines frames the whole composition; two ring forms pull toward opposite corners while magenta X-shapes and yellow bands break apart between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The internal sealed box becomes an external frame here; the enclosing line moves to the perimeter and the interior fills with competing marks.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #4

stops.whyHere: A circular mass on sky-blue, its border repeating magenta dot-flowers and zigzag bands; a single eye anchors the left while spoke-wheels pull attention right, giving watchful imbalance.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The rectangular wavy border becomes a circular one here; the interior gains a single eye, reintroducing the figure the previous works had set aside.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #175

stops.whyHere: A rounded form on teal, red rectangles tightening toward a white core; a row of white rectangles at the bottom anchors the structure with a blunt horizontal pause.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The festive circular border gives way to a compressed teal mass; the dot-flower ring is replaced by inward-tightening rectangles, and the mood shifts from watchful to dense.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #174

stops.whyHere: A looping white outline corrals organic color masses — rust, purple, olive, dark teal — while grey hatching outside the boundary reads as noise held back by that single channel.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Multiple competing outlines collapse into one looping white channel here — the enclosing line reduced to its most essential form against a field of grey scribble.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #8

chapters.title: Rhythm and Interruption
chapters.introduction: The final group tests what happens when bands meet open space or when a repeating mark is cut short, leaving the surface question unresolved.

stops.whyHere: A white zigzag and yellow waves slice the middle; two distinct zones above give way to scattered ovals below — high charge meeting sudden open space.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The continuous outline gives way to a horizontal cut; the enclosing logic breaks open and the surface splits into distinct above-and-below zones.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #141

stops.whyHere: Black ground packed with layered yellow, red, and blue zones; spirals recur at all four corners while a magenta stepped form drops through the lower center as a hinge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The horizontal split becomes a vertical drop here; the stepped magenta form replaces the zigzag cut as the image's organizing interruption.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #215

stops.whyHere: Two matching corner forms face each other across competing line types — tight zigzags, open loops, stacked rectangles — that never settle into a single rhythm.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Four-corner spirals become two mirrored forms at two corners; the internal field between them is now the site of unresolved competition.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #105

stops.whyHere: Two mismatched eye-forms anchor a frontal figure against amber; beaded blue columns contain the edges while a lower lattice of triangles and hatching reads as armored.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Abstract corner forms become recognizable eyes here, returning the figure to the surface; the competing line types below consolidate into a structured lower body.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #124

stops.whyHere: Horizontal golden bands fill the plane; descending rust discs slow the sweep while a row of blunt yellow bars at the bottom introduces a different, percussive rhythm.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The frontal figure dissolves back into pure banding; the face is gone and only the horizontal mark remains, now the whole subject.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #232

stops.whyHere: Competing zones — dark arch above, zigzag band across the middle, scattered color patches below — resist settling; no single zone holds the eye.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The calm horizontal sweep breaks apart into three zones that refuse to unify, returning the gallery's opening tension between structure and scatter.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #150

stops.whyHere: A boxy central structure of crossed circles and sawtooth borders sits in a field of restless scribbled marks; the warm gold ground holds everything loosely without resolving it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three competing zones compress into a single central structure here, but the surrounding scatter refuses to become background — the tension remains unresolved to the end.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #81

nnotb--coils-and-circles.title: Coil, Ring, Gaze
nnotb--coils-and-circles.question: When does a coiled line become an eye, and when does it stay a mark?
nnotb--coils-and-circles.introduction: Thirty works share a recurring form: the spiral, the socket, the ring. Some arrange these into faces that hold a gaze. Others scatter them across the surface until any sense of a watching presence dissolves into pattern. Moving through these rooms, the boundary between a circle that reads as an eye and one that simply repeats proves less fixed than it first appears.
nnotb--coils-and-circles.closing: Each room tested the same form — coil, ring, socket — against a different context. Whether a given circle reads as a gaze or a pattern may depend less on the mark itself than on what surrounds it.

chapters.title: Two Eyes, One Face
chapters.introduction: These works place spiral forms at eye level inside a recognizable head shape, opening the gallery's central question with the most direct evidence available.

stops.whyHere: Two square-framed spiral coils sit at eye level inside a dark rounded head; the face-reading is immediate, though loose radiating lines resist any settled calm.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #123

stops.whyHere: Twin gold spirals inside a white void ringed by black repeat the paired-eye structure; the teal field and radiating scribbles keep the figure unstable.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works place two coiled forms at eye level, but W008's amber warmth gives way here to cooler gold against flat teal, sharpening the contrast between spiral stillness and surrounding noise.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #120

stops.whyHere: Tight concentric spiral eyes dominate the upper half of a compact dark figure; the near-black ground presses the coils forward with more intensity than either predecessor.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where W103's teal field holds the figure at a distance, W217's near-black ground brings the spiral eyes close, making the coiled rings feel less decorative and more confrontational.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #80

stops.whyHere: Spiral eyes with small radiating lines sit inside a rounded head packed with layered color zones; the face is legible but crowded, the coils competing with everything around them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W217's dark ground isolates its spirals; W178 floods the same face structure with gold, teal, and red, so the coils must hold their ground against a much noisier interior.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #161

stops.whyHere: Red spiral eyes on a flat purple-blue ground give the head a diagrammatic quality; the coiled rings read as pressure rather than sight, pulling the face toward emblem.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W178's layered color interior gives way to W147's flat purple-blue field, stripping the face back to outline and spiral so the coils become more emblem than anatomy.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #228

chapters.title: Pairs and Doubles
chapters.introduction: These works place two spiral or circular forms side by side, testing whether the pairing reads as eyes, as symmetry, or as something else entirely.

stops.whyHere: Two spiral-filled squares sit side by side — one wound in warm reds, one in cooler whites — with a zigzag band between them that reads as a wide toothy opening; face-logic is present but distributed across geometric containers.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W147's single head with two red spiral eyes gives way to two separate spiral squares; the face structure is now split across distinct geometric forms rather than held inside a unified outline.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #151

stops.whyHere: Two large rectangular amber-loop forms glow side by side in the upper half; pale diagonal beams and a zigzag band below give the pairing a structural weight without resolving into a head.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W014's two spiral squares are dense and confrontational; W076's paired amber forms are warmer and more open, the loops pulling inward while pale beams push the eye downward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #77

stops.whyHere: Two square-framed spiral coils sit inside a boxed rectangular form, surrounded by dense radiating lines; the spirals hold a mechanical stillness while the outer marks press against the border.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W076's paired forms float in open space; W163 encloses its two spirals inside a drawn rectangle, adding a layer of containment that the radiating outer lines immediately contest.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #145

stops.whyHere: Two oval head-forms share the frame, each with spiral eye sockets; the warm orange grid presses against both figures so foreground and background compete at equal visual weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W163's spiral pair sits inside an abstract box; W111 returns the double structure to recognizable heads, but the grid background refuses to let the figures read as simply as faces.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #235

stops.whyHere: Two large spiral knots dominate the center without a head shape to contain them; the pairing reads as eyes or as pattern depending on where attention lands.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W111's paired spirals sit inside drawn heads; W174 removes the head entirely, leaving two spiral masses on a pale ground where the face-reading becomes optional rather than given.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #149

stops.whyHere: Two glowing concentric circles burn at center against a dark surround; pale rays push outward while competing border marks — zigzags, loops, dots — crowd every edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W174's two spirals sit in relatively open space; W267 surrounds its paired circles with dense layered marks on all sides, so the glowing cores feel pressurized rather than free.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #113

stops.whyHere: Two looping orbital forms flank a thick vertical black bar; the arrangement suggests a face without committing to one, holding both readings open simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W267's paired circles glow with clear intensity; W299 replaces that warmth with a heavy black vertical divider, making the face-reading cooler and more ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #194

chapters.title: The Circle Enclosed
chapters.introduction: Here the circular or spiral form is surrounded, contested, or crowded — held inside a boundary while the marks within press against it, making containment the visible subject.

stops.whyHere: A thick black ring holds a crowded interior — coiled yellow form, red-orange bar, white rectangular blocks — while outside marks press against the circle's edge, making containment the visible subject.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W299's face-like arrangement is open and scattered; W156 draws a hard black boundary around its interior, so the tension between inside and outside becomes explicit.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #226

stops.whyHere: A large circle ringed by small blue ovals and red dots encloses two mismatched interior zones; the dense outer ring reads as containment while yellow waves and pink drips inside push against it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W156's black ring is a single drawn outline; W136 builds its boundary from a repeating chain of small oval shapes, so the containment feels constructed mark by mark rather than imposed in one stroke.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #179

stops.whyHere: Two spiral-filled rectangles with a red cross overlay sit inside a dark field bordered by magenta dots and dash-marks; a white bar strip below introduces a sudden calm that sharpens the surrounding density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W136's circular boundary holds organic interior zones; W225 replaces the circle with rectangular containers and adds a dot-and-dash border, shifting the sense of enclosure from rounded to gridded.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #102

stops.whyHere: Two yellow-outlined spiral-filled squares sit inside a black arch edged with orange spikes; crossed boxes below and a striped oval at the base add competing layers of containment within the same frame.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W225's rectangular containers sit on a flat dark ground; W203 adds an arching black boundary above its spiral squares, layering one enclosing form inside another.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #159

stops.whyHere: A white-outlined oval on black holds dense looping lines and two contrasting eye-like forms; a cluster of marks spilling past the white edge makes the pressure from within visible.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W203's arch holds its contents; W244's oval is already breached — a cluster of marks breaks past the white boundary onto the black ground, making containment visibly incomplete.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #280

stops.whyHere: An oval on olive green holds three spiral clusters of different sizes and colors pulling in competing directions; blue diagonals and a red zigzag band cut across the lower half, spreading tension across the whole form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W244's oval sits on flat black; W184 places its oval on a warm olive field, and the interior spirals multiply rather than unify, distributing the pressure across the whole enclosed area.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #198

stops.whyHere: A rounded form on slate blue holds two coiled spirals, a red diagonal band, and stacked zigzag lines; lime and teal patches push outward against the black containment lines.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W184's oval is organic and warm-grounded; W301's enclosing form is heavier and more angular in its black outlines, giving the contained spirals a more compressed, locked quality.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #199

chapters.title: Spirals Loose in the Field
chapters.introduction: These works let circular and spiral forms scatter across the surface without a clear head or enclosing boundary, testing how far the pattern spreads before any gaze disappears.

stops.whyHere: Three spirals of different sizes hold an uneasy balance — the left one boxed, the center open, the right loose — with no single form dominating the olive-gold field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W301's spirals are locked inside a heavy outlined form; W118 releases three spirals into an open field where size and placement, not a boundary, determine their weight.

nnotb--uneven-faces.title: Scrimshaw: Two Sides of a Face
nnotb--uneven-faces.question: What visible features hold a face together when its two halves are built differently?
nnotb--uneven-faces.introduction: Every face here is split: one eye open, one crossed out; one socket a spiral, one a flat disc; one cheek warm, one cold. These thirty works move from faces where the difference is a single sharp mark to ones where the two halves appear built from entirely separate systems. Look at what holds them together — and what does not.
nnotb--uneven-faces.closing: Each face here stays in one piece despite the visible pull between its two sides. What keeps the halves from separating entirely remains a question each work answers differently.

chapters.title: One Eye Open, One Eye Not
chapters.introduction: These faces announce their asymmetry through a single sharp contrast: one eye rendered with care, the other crossed out, cancelled, or sealed. The split is immediate and frontal.

stops.whyHere: The wide concentric left eye and the crossed-out right socket state the exhibition's central problem in its most direct form.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #271

stops.whyHere: A bold red X dominates the right cheek while the left eye socket remains intact, making cancellation a large structural element rather than a small mark.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W002 crosses out one eye with hatched marks; W067 replaces that gesture with a hard red X, enlarging the erasure across the whole right side.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #184

stops.whyHere: A yellow cross on the left eye zone and a red slash on the right assign a different negation mark to each side, so neither eye escapes the cancellation logic.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W067 places one X on one side only; W090 gives each eye its own cancellation symbol, doubling the split across the face.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #125

stops.whyHere: One socket is open and ringed with petal shapes; the other is sealed by a red X — the crossed-out logic now set against a face that contains a smaller framed face inside it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W090 cancels both eyes with flat symbols; W129 restores one eye to full openness, making the X on the other side read as a deliberate contrast rather than a system applied to both.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #162

chapters.title: Spiral Against Flat
chapters.introduction: The asymmetry shifts from cancellation to construction: one eye built from coiling lines, the other from a flat fill or simple disc, the two marks disagreeing on how an eye should be made.

stops.whyHere: A wide blue-white spiral on the left faces a compact red-orange rosette on the right — two entirely different mark systems sharing the same face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W129 pairs an open petal eye with a crossed one; W221 replaces the X with a dense rosette, so both sides are now active but still built from incompatible marks.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #178

stops.whyHere: A dark inward spiral on the left and a wide outlined eye on the right pull attention in opposite directions across a yellow-gold face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W221 keeps both eye forms compact; W085 stretches the contrast — one eye collapses inward, the other opens wide into a drawn outline.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #259

stops.whyHere: A large spiral eye on the right and a smaller flat-striped eye on the left sit above a mouth traced in gold zigzag stitching, the two eye marks as different as coil and comb.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W085 sets spiral against outline on a warm ground; W130 replaces the outline eye with a flat striped form, and the pale ground makes the contrast between the two sockets starker.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #253

stops.whyHere: The left side is buried under layered scribble where an eye might be; the right opens into a tight spiral aimed at a red dot — the most extreme version of the buried-versus-revealed contrast.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W130 gives each eye a legible form; W112 removes legibility from the left side entirely, replacing it with accumulated mark-making.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #190

stops.whyHere: One eye is a deep wound of spiral lines; the other is a flat crosshatched shape — the spiral-versus-flat contrast in its most compressed, locked form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W112 buries one side under scribble; W199 replaces that scribble with a tight crossed shape, making the contrast between the two sides feel more confrontational.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #140

stops.whyHere: A coiled spiral on the left and a crosshatched rectangle on the right sit at different heights, giving the face a stacked structure built from two incompatible geometries.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W199 keeps both eye zones at roughly the same level; W200 places them at different heights, so the asymmetry becomes spatial as well as formal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #45

stops.whyHere: A golden disc eye and a concentric teal loop refuse to mirror each other; red bars slice the brow above them, adding a hard horizontal band to the organic asymmetry below.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W200 uses a warm amber ground to hold its mismatched eyes; W142 introduces a cool grey-green ground and a hard red bar, making the split feel more structural.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #230

chapters.title: Field Against Face
chapters.introduction: These works add a third element: the surrounding field presses inward, and the face must hold its asymmetry against that external density. The internal split and the outer marks work on each other.

stops.whyHere: A tightly wound right eye and a loose scrawled left eye sit inside a head that the diagonal striped background pushes against with equal visual weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W142 has a flat, contained ground; W040 surrounds its mismatched eyes with diagonal stripes that press in from every edge.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #222

stops.whyHere: Radiating blue lines converge from all sides onto a face whose two eyes are ringed in different colors; the background's agitation and the face's asymmetry reinforce each other.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W040's background stripes run parallel; W034's lines radiate inward, so the pressure feels directed at the face rather than merely surrounding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #282

stops.whyHere: A black mask holds a red spiral and a blue spiral — mismatched by color — while crossed bands of yellow, grey, and red pack the surrounding field with equal density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W034's background radiates outward from the face; W088's field is horizontal bands that neither radiate nor recede, pressing the mask flat against them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #240

stops.whyHere: Two spiral forms — one tight, one loose — sit above a red bar and a stepped white border; the rigid geometry of the surround presses against the organic asymmetry of the eye pair.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W088's background is all-over bands; W058 introduces a hard geometric border on one side only, so the surrounding pressure is itself asymmetric.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #192

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #163

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #286

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W022's surrounding tangle is dense and uniform; W071's background loops are looser and more scattered, so the pressure feels less like a wall and more like noise.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #237

chapters.title: Ornament and Asymmetry
chapters.introduction: Several faces add crowns, halos, or radiating borders that frame the uneven eyes in something ceremonial. The ornament does not resolve the split — it draws attention to it.

stops.whyHere: A spiked crown of black, purple, and yellow rises above two mismatched spiral eyes; the ceremonial headpiece and the uneven eyes sit in the same image without one explaining the other.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W071's crown is jagged points that read as alarm; W152's crown is more elaborate with added color, strengthening the ceremonial quality even as the asymmetry below it persists.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #220

stops.whyHere: A flat-topped hat caps a face split between yellow and cold teal, with two mismatched eyes below it; white-outlined hands at the edges add a further gestural element.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W152's crown rises from the head; W031's hat sits flat on top, a different kind of headgear that reads as costume rather than crown.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #294

stops.whyHere: A skull form wears yellow-gold scalloped rings around each socket — the left a plain dark oval, the right a grid of crossing lines — decorative borders that frame the asymmetry rather than hiding it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W031's hat is a flat structural cap above the face; W117's scalloped rings are applied directly to the eye sockets, so the ornament is closer to the asymmetry it frames.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #143

stops.whyHere: A circular form ringed by grey-tipped ovals and radiating yellow marks frames two mismatched eye forms — one daisy-ringed, one a spiral target — inside a halo of outward-pointing shapes.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W117's decorative rings are tight to the sockets; W189's radiating marks extend far beyond the face, making the ceremonial frame the dominant visual fact.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #217

stops.whyHere: Jagged yellow borders around each mismatched socket echo the zigzag teeth below, linking the eye asymmetry to the mouth in a single decorative system that still does not resolve the split.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W189's radiating marks push outward; W138's jagged borders stay close to the face, tightening the ornament back around the features.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #224

chapters.title: The Face as Assembled Object
chapters.introduction: The final group treats the face as a constructed thing — features locked in separate frames, color patches ignoring outlines, asymmetry a condition of how the parts were put together.

stops.whyHere: Each feature is locked inside its own framed zone — sun-circle eye, spiral eye, boxed mouth — as though the face were a cabinet of separate compartments sharing a boundary.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W138's face is unified by its decorative system; W075 breaks the face into discrete framed zones, so the asymmetry becomes structural rather than ornamental.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #279

stops.whyHere: Two mismatched orange eyes burn above a gridded mouth; striped limbs dangle at the edges, giving the face a puppet-like quality that extends the assembled feeling beyond the head itself.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W075's compartments are tightly framed within the face; W083's limbs extend beyond the body, so the assembled quality spills outside the face's boundary.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #250

stops.whyHere: A flat pink outline holds a tight red spiral and a sun-ring eye; a coiled white rod extends from the mouth, adding a mechanical component alongside the organic marks as an equal part of the assembly.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W083's extra parts are limbs; W173's extra part is a rod at the mouth, shifting the assembled quality from puppet to something more wired.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #278

stops.whyHere: Color patches float free of the drawn outlines, so the face reads as two overlapping systems — one drawn, one painted — sharing a space without fully merging; the oversized left eye and smaller right eye make the mismatch visible at the level of drawing itself.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W173's assembly is additive, with parts attached; W143's assembly is layered, with drawn and painted systems occupying the same space independently.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #293

stops.whyHere: A tight white spiral and a looping pink flower mark two eye zones inside a large outlined form; wave lines pile up inside and outside the boundary, so the face and its field are made from the same marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W143's two systems stay within the face outline; W160's marks spill beyond it, dissolving the boundary between the assembled face and the space around it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #223

stops.whyHere: A coiling spiral on the left and a jagged triangular tangle on the right are built from opposite geometries; the face pushes to the frame edges, and the bared teeth below read as the one fixed point in an otherwise unresolved assembly.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W160's boundary dissolves into its field; W181 reasserts a strong outer edge while keeping the interior split between two incompatible geometries.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #209

stops.whyHere: Dense scribble lines pile up differently around each eye — one heavily shadowed, one sitting higher with a pale surround — while surrounding color bursts feel raw and separate from the face, an honest contrast to the more structured assemblies preceding it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W181 holds its form through a strong outer edge; W012 has no such containment — the face pushes to the picture edge and the surrounding marks feel unresolved, ending the gallery on a note of open asymmetry.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #260
