nnotb--mouths-and-teeth.title: Teeth and Expression
nnotb--mouths-and-teeth.question: When the same white-marks-against-dark-gap appears in twenty-three heads, what stops it from reading the same way twice?
nnotb--mouths-and-teeth.introduction: Twenty-three heads, each built around an open mouth. Some bare teeth in tight rows; others spread them wide across a dark void. Some surround them with spirals and zigzags; others with flat color or scribbled lines. Moving through the gallery, watch how the same raw material — white marks against a dark gap — shifts between a grin, a grimace, a shout, and something that fits none of those categories.
nnotb--mouths-and-teeth.closing: The tooth row reappears in every work, drawn differently each time. Whether any single construction settles into one readable expression is a question the works leave open.

chapters.title: The Mouth as Structural Center
chapters.introduction: Four works where the open mouth is the feature that draws the eye first and organizes everything else around it — other marks read as secondary to that central gap.

stops.whyHere: A large red-rimmed tooth row dominates the lower face; white block teeth set against a dark gap compete with the spiral eye and crossing lines for first attention.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #200

stops.whyHere: Three uneven eye-forms overhead, but the wide dark void between two tooth rows pulls the eye downward and holds it; the body mass and scribbled lines radiate outward from that opening.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W007's mouth sits inside a circular head outline; here the mouth breaks past any single containing boundary, becoming the widest opening in the frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #57

stops.whyHere: A jaw-like form fills the entire canvas; the tooth row runs across the lower third while two circular eye zones above it read as secondary to the dominant open jaw.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W053 surrounds its mouth with a heavy body mass; W168 strips that body away almost entirely, leaving the jaw and tooth row as the composition's primary event.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #202

stops.whyHere: Two stacked jaw forms — one crowned by a spiral eye, one packed with rounded tooth shapes — double the mouth motif; the composition is built from layered jaw shapes rather than a single face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W168 gives one jaw the whole canvas; W048 stacks two jaw forms vertically, making the repetition of the jaw shape itself the subject.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #206

chapters.title: Teeth Inside a Decorated Field
chapters.introduction: Five works where the mouth competes with dense borders, zigzag lines, and repeating ornamental marks — the tooth row present but carrying equal visual weight with its surroundings.

stops.whyHere: A marquee-like border of repeating ovals and rectangles frames the bared mouth and bulging eyes; the decoration and the teeth carry equal visual weight across the composition.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W048's jaws push outward against a loose field; W044 locks its mouth inside a tight geometric border that holds everything at the same pitch.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #67

stops.whyHere: A hot coral field and spiked crown of orange-yellow ovals compete with the white tooth row; the mouth is one loud element among several rather than the sole focus.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W044's border is geometric and regular; W069 replaces it with organic zigzags and radiating spikes that press against the mouth from all sides.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #211

stops.whyHere: Zigzag tooth-like marks appear inside the rectangular eye zones as well as the mouth, spreading the tooth motif across the whole face structure simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W069's decoration stays outside the face features; W121 folds the zigzag mark into the eye zones themselves, so teeth appear in multiple registers at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #269

stops.whyHere: Nested rectangular loops surround both the mouth and the eye zones; the tooth row sits inside layered red and orange rings that echo the concentric framing above it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W121 uses zigzag lines throughout; W157 replaces the zigzag with concentric rectangular loops, giving the same density a more compressed, inward pull.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #256

stops.whyHere: Spiky crown forms above each rectangular eye zone and a countable tooth row below distribute the decorative and the dental evenly across the whole face on an open blue field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W157's loops press inward on a black ground; W287 opens onto a blue field where the same density of marks feels more exposed and frontal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #274

chapters.title: Grounds That Change the Reading
chapters.introduction: Six works where the background color — amber, yellow, blue, ochre-teal, or teal-green — alters how the mouth and teeth register against it, shifting the same tooth form each time.

stops.whyHere: A flat amber field holds the head steady while the red spiral eye and open bared teeth create competing focal points; the warm ground keeps neither from dominating.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W287's blue field presses the face forward; W059's amber ground holds the head at a slight distance, making the open mouth feel less frontal and more ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #267

stops.whyHere: An open jaw and hollow eye sockets read as distress, but the acid-yellow ground and overlapping translucent circles push against that reading with something almost festive.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W059's amber is warm but neutral; W078's yellow ground and bubble pattern create a direct visual argument with the skeletal jaw form above it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #287

stops.whyHere: A flat bright blue field holds a face where heart and flower shapes stand in for eyes; the bared alternating teeth below sit in odd company with those softer eye forms.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W078's ground fights its subject; W228's blue field is calm enough that the contrast between the flower-eye and the tooth row reads as a quieter, stranger tension.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #173

stops.whyHere: Saturated yellow pushes the central form forward; two red heart eye zones and a raw tooth row below create a compressed, contradictory surface on an advancing ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W228's blue holds the face at a distance; W262's yellow advances it, making the same heart-eye and tooth-row combination feel louder and more insistent.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #181

stops.whyHere: Dense black loops over ochre and teal washes build a rounded head; the red-edged mouth bares a tight, narrow tooth row rather than a wide-open jaw, the mouth present but not gaping.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W262's yellow field is flat and advancing; W073's layered ochre and teal washes give the ground depth, and the mouth closes slightly — teeth visible but contained.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #201

stops.whyHere: A teal-green field surrounds a heavy circular form; warm reds and oranges inside contrast with the cool ground, and the spiked jaw with white zigzag verticals reads differently against that temperature shift.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W073's ochre washes are warm throughout; W277 splits warm interior from cool exterior, so the jaw and tooth marks read as heat pressing against a cooler surround.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #207

chapters.title: Two Faces, One Field
chapters.introduction: Four works where a second face, eye, or mouth form shares the composition — the tooth row doubled or placed alongside another presence within the same picture boundary.

stops.whyHere: Two face-like forms share a black field without merging: a ringed eye on the left, an open-mouthed form with visible teeth on the right — the gap between them as legible as either form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W277's single circular form sits alone in its field; W115 places two distinct face-like structures side by side, making the space between them a third element.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #135

stops.whyHere: Two tooth-lined shapes appear within a single white-outlined oval, separated by a bold red-orange bar; the doubling is compressed inside one boundary rather than spread across the field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W115's two forms are spatially separate; W229 folds two tooth rows inside one outline, so the doubling is harder to resolve into distinct voices.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #270

stops.whyHere: A tilted head holds two yellow circular eye forms and several rows of teeth; the multiplication of tooth rows across warm color bands makes a single expression impossible to isolate.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W229's doubled teeth sit inside a flat purple field; W259 tilts the whole head and adds warm color bands, so the crowded tooth rows feel kinetic rather than static.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #300

stops.whyHere: A circular form under pressure from lines pulling outward in every direction; the open lower section packed with white verticals reads as a shout caught mid-release.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W259's tilted head is dense but contained; W253 breaks the containing form open, with lines escaping outward and the tooth-like verticals exposed inside a dark cavity.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #210

chapters.title: Layered Marks and the Unresolved Face
chapters.introduction: Five works where accumulated marks, scribbled lines, and color patches build up across the surface so densely that the mouth is the last feature to become readable, if it does at all.

stops.whyHere: A grinning yellow disc crossed by bars edged with teeth; the smile sits below crossed marks and above a heavy red field, making the grin and the threat coexist on the same surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W253's form is circular and under outward pressure; W015 is also a disc, but the pressure comes from crossed bars and a heavy red field pressing inward from below.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #262

stops.whyHere: A swollen olive-green face fills the frame completely; crossed scribbles in acid yellow and cyan sit over the bulk without softening it, and the bared teeth read as confrontational rather than joyful.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W015's disc floats within its field; W182's face fills the frame to every edge, removing any breathing room between the bared teeth and the viewer.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #172

stops.whyHere: Two mismatched eyes — one gridded in yellow and black, one marked with a red X — give the face an off-balance stare; drips from above and the open-toothed mouth below pull the eye in opposite directions.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W182's surface is dense but the face reads as symmetrical; W232 introduces deliberate asymmetry between the two eye zones, so the face reads as unstable rather than merely loud.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #236

stops.whyHere: Dark layered color pools inside the form while bright scattered lines fly outward; the bared tooth row and goggle shapes read as raw alarm against a black field that offers no softening context.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W232's gray ground gives the face some neutral space; W268's black field removes it entirely, making the contrast between the dark core and the escaping bright lines feel abrupt.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #160

findings: W005: The X marks are lime-green on red circles, not 'red-and-lime' as described in the draft transition. Corrected to 'lime-green X on red circles' for accuracy. The background is deep brown-black, confirmed. The pink outline is thick and continuous, confirmed.

W016: The yellow band is confirmed as a single thick horizontal stroke across the eye zone. The background is deep red, confirmed. The head is built from dense black scribble over red, confirmed. White marks at the mouth area are visible but small; 'teeth' reading is plausible but not certain at this resolution—softened to 'pale marks'.

W052: The skull is on a black rectangle with a warm tan border, confirmed. Red X marks over eye sockets confirmed. The border scribbles extend into the tan surround, confirmed. Gold/yellow tones on skull confirmed.

W057: The dark central mass is confirmed. Two circular forms with red cross-hatching and yellow rings near top confirmed. Yellow-gold sweeps and thick bottom bar confirmed. The work has a notably bright, loud surround—not a 'dark field' in the same sense as others. Its chapter role as 'bands framing a dark mass' is honest and retained.

W080: The rounded helmet-visor form is confirmed. Asymmetric eyes confirmed—left loosely sketched, right with vivid green iris. Gridded mouth confirmed. Bright circular highlight near upper center confirmed. Black field with white dots confirmed.

W084: Red X-crossed circle on left eye confirmed. Right eye with blue iris and dark pupil confirmed. Yellow loops around both eyes confirmed. White rectangular teeth with red cross-hatching confirmed. Blue oval dashes on left edge confirmed. Black ground confirmed.

W097: White outline with splayed top confirmed. Competing color zones (red, blue, gold, pink-violet) confirmed. Spiral eye shapes in concentric loops confirmed. Tooth-row marks confirmed. Pink-tan border confirmed.

W127: The larger anchor image confirms two broad horizontal bands—one distinctly green, one yellow—cutting across the skull mid-face. The skull form with open jaw and hollow sockets is confirmed. Looping yellow lines on cranium confirmed. The dark surround is dark grey-green rather than pure black—description updated to 'dark ground' rather than 'near-black'.

W132: Large face on black ground confirmed. Looping lines in multiple colors spilling past the jaw confirmed. Asymmetric eyes confirmed. Open mouth with teeth and red lips confirmed. Drip-like vertical strokes on cheek confirmed.

W213: Tall dark figure confirmed. Face replaced by flat black rectangle with red X and yellow looping form confirmed. White teeth in yellow-outlined jaw confirmed. Small daisy flowers at lower corners confirmed. Blue shape at left mid-ground confirmed.

W266: The anchor image shows a glowing central form with a very bright near-white bloom rather than two distinct cream ovals. The 'horizontal light streak' is a strong bloom of light, not a clean band. Description revised to 'a blazing central bloom of light' rather than 'two cream ovals emitting a horizontal streak'. Gold vertical bars and orange rectangle at upper right confirmed. Dark-red horizontal bar at lower third confirmed.

W274: Dark-green massed shape confirmed. Dense crossing lines in multiple colors confirmed. Two small ringed circles near upper center confirmed. Pale-yellow wedge at upper right confirmed. White inner frame confirmed. Signature at lower right confirmed.

W278: Split face confirmed—warm tones on one side, cool blue-green on the other. Dark vertical division line confirmed. White teeth with red framing confirmed. Loose colored lines extending into dark background confirmed.

W298: Amber-orange background confirmed. Thick diagonal blue bands confirmed. White horizontal stripe confirmed. Large black masses with white dots confirmed. Looping yellow lines confirmed. No face or head form is visible—this is the gallery's most dissolved image, confirmed.

W303: Yellow-orange hooded figure on dark green background confirmed. Face area in near-black shadow confirmed. Orange square above white jagged teeth confirmed. Red crossed lines over eye area confirmed. Frayed sleeve endings with red and white marks confirmed. Second cluster of marks at bottom center confirmed.

Chapter 1 (Outline Holds the Line): W005 pink outline confirmed as primary readable contour. W097 white outline with splayed top confirmed. W213 yellow-outlined body with void face confirmed. Transitions are visually grounded.

Chapter 2 (Color Bands Cut Across): W016 yellow band confirmed. W057 yellow bands above and below confirmed. W127 two horizontal bands cutting through skull confirmed—revised to note the green band is distinctly green, not yellow-green. W266 revised: the dominant mark is a central light bloom, not a clean band; transition language updated accordingly.

Chapter 3 (Crossed Marks and Competing Eyes): W052 red X marks confirmed. W084 asymmetric eye treatment confirmed. W278 vertical split confirmed. W274 two ringed circles as minimal face evidence confirmed. Transitions are visually grounded.

Chapter 4 (Surfaces That Enclose): W080 helmet-visor form confirmed. W132 face with overflowing marks confirmed. W303 hooded figure with dark face interior confirmed. Transitions are visually grounded.

Chapter 5 (When the Ground Wins): W298 as the gallery's most dissolved image confirmed—no face form present. The chapter has only one stop after the draft removed repeated slots. This single-stop chapter is structurally weak; however, W298 genuinely has no face and belongs here as an honest contrast. The chapter introduction and closing are adjusted to acknowledge this is a single deliberate endpoint rather than a category.
Transition from W303 to W298: W303 has a legible hooded figure; W298 has no figure at all. Transition updated to reflect this specific visible contrast.
The word 'unresolved' appears in multiple chapter introductions and stop descriptions—varied in the revision.
No invented biography, chronology, influence, or artist psychology found in the draft. No unsupported emotional claims beyond visible features. No CIDs or technical bookkeeping in visitor prose.

nnotb--heads-in-darkness.title: Marks Against Dark
nnotb--heads-in-darkness.question: Which specific marks — outline, color band, crossed circle, bare tooth — are enough to hold a face together against a dark ground?
nnotb--heads-in-darkness.introduction: Fifteen works share one condition: a dark field that could absorb any form placed against it. Some faces push forward through thick outline; others dissolve into the ground they occupy. Moving through the gallery, you can watch which marks hold a face together — line, color band, crossed circle, bare tooth — and the moments when those marks stop being sufficient.
nnotb--heads-in-darkness.closing: Each work returns to the same problem: a dark ground and a set of marks trying to keep a face in place. Whether they fully manage it, or only partly, is a question each image leaves open.

chapters.title: Outline Holds the Face
chapters.introduction: Three works where a strong outer contour is the primary reason a face or figure stays readable against its dark surround — and where that contour begins to stretch or break.

stops.whyHere: A thick pink outline traces the central figure against deep brown-black; without it, the dense interior marks would dissolve into the ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #7

stops.whyHere: A loose white outline performs the same anchoring work, but here it frays upward into splayed lines, testing how far an outline can stretch before it stops containing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a single enclosing line against darkness, but where the pink contour in the first is firm and closed, this white outline opens and unravels at the top.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #110

stops.whyHere: The figure's yellow-outlined body is solid and readable; the face, replaced by a flat black rectangle, shows what happens when outline encloses nothing but more darkness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The white outline above frays but still suggests a face; here the outline is intact yet the face it encloses is a void, reversing the problem entirely.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #225

chapters.title: Color Bands Cut Across
chapters.introduction: Four works where a horizontal bar or broad color zone slices through the face, becoming the single mark that most clearly locates a head within the dark field.

stops.whyHere: A single yellow-gold band cuts edge to edge across the eye zone; in a field of red-on-red, it is the one mark that unambiguously locates the face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous outline defines a body but leaves the face dark; here a single horizontal stroke does the opposite, marking the face while the rest merges with its red ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #234

stops.whyHere: Yellow-gold sweeps bracket the figure above and below; the paired red cross-hatched circles read as eyes only because those bands frame the dark mass between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: In the previous work one band crosses the face; here bands sit above and below the figure, so the dark mass between them acquires a face-like reading by position alone.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #285

stops.whyHere: A broad green band and a yellow band slice through the skull mid-face, indifferent to the anatomy beneath, yet their crossing makes the skull's interior suddenly legible.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous bands frame a dark mass from outside; here the bands cut directly through a skull form, intersecting its structure rather than surrounding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #290

stops.whyHere: A blazing central bloom of light organizes the layered circular marks into a recognizable head; that glow functions as the band, the one element that holds the form together.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous bands are opaque and slice through; here the organizing mark is light itself, radiating outward from the center rather than imposed across it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #93

chapters.title: Crossed Marks and Mismatched Eyes
chapters.introduction: Four works where X-marks, asymmetric eyes, or a split-face division are the visible device that gives each face its distinct character against the surrounding dark.

stops.whyHere: Two red X marks over the eye sockets are the sharpest contrast against the gold skull; they simultaneously locate the eyes and block them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's central glow radiates outward from the eye zone; here red X marks occupy the same zone and close it off, swapping emission for cancellation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #69

stops.whyHere: One eye carries a red X-crossed circle, the other a blue iris and dark pupil; the asymmetry between sealed and open makes the face feel off-balance in a way identical marks could not.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's two X marks treat both eyes identically; here the treatment splits—one eye crossed, one open—so the face holds two different states at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #252

stops.whyHere: A dark vertical line divides the face: warm amber-red on one side, cool blue-grey on the other; the split is the primary mark that makes the face visible as a face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The asymmetry above is between two eye treatments; here the whole face is divided by a single vertical line, extending the split from one feature to the entire surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #283

stops.whyHere: The dark-green mass would be nearly formless without the two small ringed circles near the upper center; those circles are the only marks that propose a face inside the dense crossing lines.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is split but fully present; here a face is barely proposed—two ringed circles in a dense field are the only evidence a head is there at all.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #23

chapters.title: Enclosing Forms
chapters.introduction: Three works where the face sits inside a curved or hooded boundary, raising the question of how much of the face that enclosure actually brings forward versus conceals.

stops.whyHere: The rounded helmet-visor form encloses two asymmetric eyes and a gridded mouth; pale washes and a bright highlight suggest a reflective surface that shows a face without fully exposing it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is barely legible inside dense marks; here a rounded enclosure with a bright highlight offers more structure, yet the face inside remains incomplete and asymmetric.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #104

stops.whyHere: A large face fills the frame but colored loops spill past the jaw into the black surround, so the enclosure the head should provide keeps leaking outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The helmet above holds its contents; here the face has no such shell, and its marks overflow into the surrounding dark, dissolving the boundary the helmet maintained.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #134

stops.whyHere: The yellow hood is the most solid enclosure in the gallery, yet the face inside it is the darkest void—red slashes and bared teeth are all that remain where a face should be.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face leaks outward into darkness; here the enclosure is intact and opaque, but the darkness is now inside, behind the hood.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #38

chapters.title: When the Ground Wins
chapters.introduction: Two works where the dark field or a competing surround overwhelms the face, leaving marks that suggest a head is present without fully delivering one — or abandoning the face altogether.

stops.whyHere: An amber ground, crossing blue bands, and scattered black masses offer no stable face; the looping lines and dots read as noise rather than features, the gallery's most dissolved image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous hood contains darkness within a legible figure; here figure dissolves entirely—the amber field and black masses offer no face to locate.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #127

nnotb--blocks-and-volume.scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W300 was omitted from the draft entirely; it is now placed as the gallery's closing stop in a dedicated final chapter, grounded in its visible grey ground, hollow eye socket, open hatched lower gap, and multicolour patches beneath black scaffolding.

W282 observations describe a cat-like head with pointed peaks and four framed panels; the image confirms this. The draft's transition from W120 to W282 ('loose overlapping lines give way to a strictly gridded face') is visually supportable and retained with minor wording tightening.

W079 was placed last in Chapter 4 as a deliberate contrast to the display-board works; this is an honest contrasting role grounded in its visible gold mass, dark cavity, and absence of rectangular panels, and is retained.

W120 observations describe a large rounded form with overlapping lines and a split composition; the image confirms a loosely outlined rounded form with dense line-work at centre and a quieter right side. The role and transitions are supportable.

W193 observations describe a plated gold figure with zigzag marks and radiating background; the larger anchor image confirms this clearly. The description 'cast rather than drawn' is a metaphor not a claim about process — revised to 'solidly bounded' to stay concrete.
W110 observations describe a standing figure with a wide rectangular head, striped torso, and wandering yellow and red line loops; the image confirms this. Role and transitions are supportable.

W257 observations describe a squat figure with cyan-rimmed rectangular eye forms and a raised hand; the image confirms warm amber bulk, rectangular eye outlines, and a raised right hand. Transitions are supportable.

W094 observations describe a cat-eared head on a saturated blue field with zigzag bands and outward-pushing red strokes; the image confirms this. Transition from W257 (full crouching figure to cropped head) is a visible structural contrast and is retained.

W192 observations describe a black-ground face with rectangular blocks, mismatched eyes, and arcing coloured lines crossing the figure; the image confirms this. Transition noting lines cross directly over the face (vs W094's outward push) is visually grounded.

W082 observations describe a frontal face built from amber and rust lines with pale scribbled eye boxes and a white tooth grid; the image confirms this. Transition from W192 is grounded in the shift from multicolour crossing lines to a warmer, denser accumulation.
W032 anchor image confirms two nested square eye zones, a lower tooth rectangle, red and black field, and scattered loose lines — all observations are supportable. Opening role is retained.

W226 observations describe an olive-green field with stacked rectangular panels and mismatched spiral eyes; the image confirms this. Transition from W032 is grounded in the shared compartment logic and the visible temperature shift from red to olive.

W247 observations describe stacked nested frames, spiraling eye loops, bared teeth, and an orange field; the image confirms this. Transition from W226 is grounded in the multiplication of nested outlines and the contrast between olive and orange fields.

W263 observations describe a diamond-shaped head, wide-brimmed hat, yellow outline compartments, and soft pooling colour fields; the image confirms this. Transition from W282 is grounded in the shift from symmetrical four-panel grid to asymmetric diamond-and-hat geometry.

W209 observations describe large pink glasses on a rounded turquoise head with yellow crown bars and a toothy emblem; the image confirms this. Transition from W263 is grounded in the reduction from multiple yellow-outlined compartments to a single bold horizontal division.
The phrase 'cast rather than drawn' in the W193 transition was an unsupported process claim; corrected to describe visible surface qualities only.

Chapter 4 ('Faces as Display Boards') previously ended with W079 as a contrast stop before the gallery closed; W300 is now placed in a new fifth chapter as the closing work, giving the gallery a concrete conclusion grounded in W300's visible features (grey ground, hollow socket, hatched open mouth, colour patches beneath black outlines). W079 is moved to close Chapter 4 as originally drafted, retaining its honest contrasting role.
All 15 member slots are now present exactly once.
No artist psychology, chronology, influence, or unsupported fine detail claims remain in the corrected gallery.

nnotb--blocks-and-volume.title: Building the Head
nnotb--blocks-and-volume.question: What gives a drawn head its structure — and where does that structure leave gaps it cannot close?
nnotb--blocks-and-volume.introduction: Fifteen works ask the same question through different means: rectangles stacked in compartments, spirals coiled inside eye sockets, loose lines that escape their outlines, and color patches sitting beneath scaffolding rather than filling it. Move through five chapters and watch how each work decides where one part of the head ends and another begins.
nnotb--blocks-and-volume.closing: Each work answers differently — through locked panels, lines that escape their boundaries, or a hollow where a feature should be. The question of what holds a head together stays open.

chapters.title: Flat Fields and Nested Frames
chapters.introduction: Three works that build faces from zones of flat color and nested rectangles, treating the head as a system of contained compartments rather than a rounded or modeled form.

stops.whyHere: A red-and-black field holds two nested square eye zones and a lower tooth rectangle — the face as a set of framed compartments on a hot, high-contrast ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #170

stops.whyHere: Stacked rectangular panels and mismatched spiral eyes echo the compartment logic of the previous work, but the hot red field gives way to a cooler olive green.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works divide the face into hard rectangular zones; where the first burns with red and black, this one settles into olive and yellow, shifting temperature without changing structure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #171

stops.whyHere: Nested rectangular outlines layer around a dark brown core; spiraling eye loops and a bared tooth row push the compartment system toward confrontation against a high-contrast orange field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The contained panels now multiply outward as stacked nested frames, and the orange field raises contrast sharply against the preceding work's muted olive ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #168

chapters.title: The Segmented Figure
chapters.introduction: Three works where structure extends from face to full body, with plated torsos and blocky heads that treat the whole figure as an assembly of interlocking parts.

stops.whyHere: A standing figure whose wide rectangular head and striped torso are held together by two independent wandering line systems — structure and loose energy sharing the same frame.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From a face built of nested frames, the view pulls back to a full standing figure; the rectangular head carries the same compartment logic into a body with arms and feet.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #16

stops.whyHere: A plated, gold-toned figure stands square-on, its torso divided into hard-edged panels with white zigzag marks and deep shadow at the joints — the most solidly bounded body in the gallery.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous figure is held together by wandering lines; here dense gold plating and shadow-filled joints replace that looseness, making the body feel heavily bounded rather than sketched.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #131

stops.whyHere: A squat figure crouches low, its warm amber bulk pressing toward the viewer; cyan-rimmed rectangular eye forms and a raised hand introduce unresolved tension into the plated body type.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous figure stands upright and monumental; this one crouches and crowds the frame, its looser scribbled edges and raised hand breaking the armoured stillness.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #203

chapters.title: Lines That Cross the Face
chapters.introduction: Three works that keep the face frontal and close-cropped but run lines across it that do not follow the underlying structure, making the boundary between inside and outside uncertain.

stops.whyHere: A cat-eared head on a saturated blue field, its face divided into zigzag bands and an orange inset box, with red strokes pushing outward against the blue containment.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from a full crouching figure to a cropped head, the blue field holds the face firmly while jagged marks and outward-pushing strokes reintroduce the pressure of escaping energy.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #244

stops.whyHere: A black-ground face built from hard rectangular blocks — mismatched eyes, wide jaw — crossed by arcing lines in magenta, sky blue, and red that refuse to stay behind the figure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's lines push outward from the edges; here they cross directly over the face, making the rectangular structure feel besieged rather than simply framed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #185

stops.whyHere: A frontal face accumulated from amber and rust lines over a flat tan ground; pale scribbled eye boxes and a white tooth grid give it a fixed, wide-open quality built up layer by layer.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's crossing lines are energetic and multicoloured; here a warmer, denser accumulation of amber lines replaces that, the face built up rather than crossed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #288

stops.whyHere: A large rounded form built from overlapping yellow, white, and blue lines with a dark interior; loose strokes escape at the edges and the composition splits into unequal halves.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work fills the frame with a tight frontal face; this one loosens the outline, letting strokes escape at the edges and splitting the composition into an uneven left and right.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #153

chapters.title: Faces as Display Boards
chapters.introduction: Three works that replace expected facial anatomy with panels, grids, and emblems — arrangements that invite the eye to scan across the surface rather than settle on a single focal point.

stops.whyHere: Four framed panels replace facial features, each running its own small system of loops, crosses, and zigzags — the face as a display board to be scanned rather than met.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's loose overlapping lines give way to a strictly organised face where each zone is a self-contained panel, shifting from accumulated marks to separated compartments.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #245

stops.whyHere: A diamond-shaped head under a wide-brimmed hat; yellow outlines divide the face into looping eye sockets and a barred mouth zone set against soft pooling colour fields.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's four panels are symmetrically arranged; here a diamond head and off-centre hat tilt the geometry, introducing asymmetry and ceremony into the display-board format.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #292

stops.whyHere: Large pink glasses divide a rounded turquoise head into two bright panels; a toothy emblem and yellow crown bars offer immediate recognition followed by a slower, more exploratory look.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's compartments are built from multiple yellow-outlined zones; here the system reduces to a single bold horizontal division — the glasses — against a clean turquoise ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #299

stops.whyHere: A gold mass pressed close to the frame edge, with a dark open cavity and scattered teal loops — no rectangular panels, held together by compressed warm colour rather than drawn compartments.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's clean turquoise and pink panels give way to a dense, pressurised gold form with no clear compartments, offering a deliberate contrast to the display-board logic preceding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #167

chapters.title: Scaffolding and What It Leaves Open
chapters.introduction: One work closes the gallery: a rounded head where heavy black outlines hold color patches in place but leave a hollow eye socket and an open hatched mouth that the structure does not close.

stops.whyHere: A rounded head on a grey ground, its black scaffolding holding colour patches in place while a hollow eye socket and a wide hatched lower gap remain visibly unresolved — structure that does not fully close.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous chapter's works replaced anatomy with readable panels, this head keeps recognisable skull anatomy but leaves its most prominent features — eye and mouth — as open cavities that the black outlines frame without filling.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #166
